Most tipped the left ear (81%) by visual estimation, the median post-hemostasis bleeding rate was 5%, and techniques varied without a clearly superior method
There was one standard technique
mcqs.e: Nearly all respondents recognised the ear tip as indicating sterilisation.

title: Characteristics of cat semi-owners
authors: Ma GC, McLeod LJ, Zito SJ
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
citation: Ma GC, McLeod LJ, Zito SJ Characteristics of cat semi-owners. Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery. 2023. doi:10.1177/1098612X231194225
abstract: The study examined people who care for stray cats without considering themselves owners. Researchers surveyed 8,708 New South Wales residents, finding that 588 respondents (7%) were 'semi-owners' of unowned cats. These individuals were significantly more likely to be female, urban-dwelling, from lower socioeconomic areas, and renting their homes. Notably, most semi-owners also owned their own cats and had more cats than non-semi-owners. The researchers concluded that semi-owners represent an important target audience for behavior change interventions aimed at managing cat populations, but interventions must acknowledge barriers like cost and trust issues.

mcqs.q: A survey of 8,708 New South Wales residents identified 'semi-owners' of unowned cats (7%). Which finding is correct?
o: They were more likely to be female, urban, renting and from lower socioeconomic areas, and most also owned cats, making them a target for behaviour change
They were mostly male rural landowners
They did not own any cats of their own
mcqs.e: Interventions must acknowledge barriers such as cost and trust.

title: Feline chaphamaparvovirus (feline fechavirus) in different cat populations
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
citation: Weese JS, MacNicol J Feline chaphamaparvovirus (feline fechavirus) in different cat populations. Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery. 2026. doi:10.1177/1098612X261428723
abstract: The researchers assessed the presence of feline chaphamaparvovirus (FeChPV) across various feline populations. They gathered fecal and vomitus samples from 136 cats across multiple facilities: 65 from a shelter without apparent gastrointestinal disease, 25 from shelters experiencing vomiting/diarrhea clusters, and 46 from a research colony following a recent outbreak. Testing revealed FeChPV in 30 of 136 samples (22%). Infection rates varied by location: 12% in the asymptomatic shelter, 11-25% in affected shelters, and 88% in one shelter with acute disease. Notably, the virus appeared in both symptomatic cats (33% of diarrheic animals) and healthy ones (17% of non-symptomatic cats). The researchers concluded that while FeChPV correlates with facility outbreaks, its precise pathogenic role remains ambiguous since detection occurred in healthy populations.

mcqs.q: Feline chaphamaparvovirus was tested in 136 cats from shelters and a research colony. What was concluded about its role?
o: It is a proven cause of diarrhoea in every infected cat
It was found only in cats with diarrhoea
It correlates with facility outbreaks but was also found in healthy cats (17%), so its pathogenic role is unclear
mcqs.e: Overall detection was 22%, and 88% in one shelter with acute disease.

title: Effects of intranasal maropitant on clinical signs of naturally acquired upper respiratory disease in shelter cats
authors: Parncutt J, Johnson LR, Subharat S, Oke B, Hill KE
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
citation: Parncutt J, Johnson LR, Subharat S, Oke B, Hill KE Effects of intranasal maropitant on clinical signs of naturally acquired upper respiratory disease in shelter cats. Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery. 2025. doi:10.1177/1098612X241309826
abstract: The research team investigated whether intranasal maropitant citrate could reduce severity of feline upper respiratory disease (FURD) in shelter settings. Sixty-one cats received either intranasal maropitant (34 cats) or saline placebo (27 cats) twice daily for seven days. Clinical assessments measured conjunctivitis, blepharospasm, ocular discharge, and nasal discharge using visual analogue scales at baseline and completion. Key finding: there was no significant difference in clinical index scores between the maropitant treatment and control groups for conjunctivitis, blepharospasm, ocular discharge, nasal discharge or total disease severity after 7 days. The researchers concluded that intranasal maropitant showed no clinical benefit compared to saline treatment, and found no evidence to support the routine use of intranasal maropitant in managing feline upper respiratory disease.

mcqs.q: Sixty-one shelter cats with upper respiratory disease received intranasal maropitant or saline twice daily for 7 days. What was found?
o: Maropitant significantly reduced nasal discharge
No significant difference in clinical scores, so there is no evidence to support routine use
Maropitant worsened conjunctivitis
mcqs.e: Conjunctivitis, blepharospasm, ocular discharge and nasal discharge were scored with visual analogue scales.

title: Randomized, non-inferiority clinical trial of three topical dermatophytosis treatments in shelter cats
authors: DeTar L, Janke KJ, Jacobson L
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
citation: DeTar L, Janke KJ, Jacobson L Randomized, non-inferiority clinical trial of three topical dermatophytosis treatments in shelter cats. Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery. 2025. doi:10.1177/1098612X251360611
abstract: This prospective randomized trial evaluated three topical antifungal treatments for cats with Microsporum canis infections in shelter settings. All cats received oral itraconazole while being assigned to one of three topical groups: lime sulfur (LS), miconazole chlorhexidine (MC), or hydrogen peroxide (HP) shampoo. The study enrolled 76 cats across four US shelters. Lime sulfur significantly outperformed alternatives, achieving mycological cure by 7 weeks in all treated cats, compared to 62.5% of MC-treated and 78.3% of HP-treated cats. Mean time to cure was 27 days for LS versus 37 days for MC and 36 days for HP. Younger cats required longer treatment periods. Staff noted no meaningful differences between products regarding application difficulty or feline tolerance, though some side effects were documented including bleached hair (HP) and hypothermia (MC and HP). The researchers concluded that while LS demonstrated superior efficacy, hydrogen peroxide represents an acceptable alternative to lime sulfur if preferred.

mcqs.q: Cats with Microsporum canis infection received oral itraconazole plus lime sulfur, miconazole-chlorhexidine, or hydrogen peroxide shampoo. Which result is correct?
o: Miconazole-chlorhexidine was best, curing all cats by 7 weeks
All three gave identical cure rates and times
Lime sulfur gave mycological cure in all cats by 7 weeks (versus 62.5% and 78.3%), and hydrogen peroxide was an acceptable alternative
mcqs.e: Mean time to cure was 27 days for lime sulfur versus 37 and 36 days, and side effects included bleached hair and hypothermia.

title: The effect of animal shelter sound on cat behaviour and welfare
authors: Eagan BH, Gordon E, Fraser D
citation: Eagan BH, Gordon E, Fraser D The effect of animal shelter sound on cat behaviour and welfare. Animal Welfare. 2021. doi:10.7120/09627286.30.4.006
abstract: This investigation assessed how sound affected fearand maintenance-related behaviors in single-housed shelter cats. Two daily 30-minute observation sessions (morning and evening) occurred for 98 cats over ten days. Cat behaviour and presence of sound (classified by source) were recorded by instantaneous and one-zero sampling with 15-second intervals. Sessions were classified as 'quiet' or 'noisy' based on median sound levels. Statistical analysis included 70 cats with adequate comparable observations. Males demonstrated less fear and maintenance behavior than females. Morning sessions consistently had much more sound than evenings, and cats showed more fear behaviour and less maintenance behaviour in the mornings. Cats exhibited more fear responses during noisy morning sessions compared to quiet ones. When sound transitioned from quiet to noisy, fear-related behaviour increased; transitions from noisy to quiet showed decreased fear behaviours. The findings indicate that shelter cats vary significantly in responsiveness, and environmental sound substantially influences their conduct. The researchers conclude that reducing shelter noise levels may enhance overall welfare outcomes for cats.

mcqs.q: Sound was recorded during observation of 98 single-housed shelter cats. Which finding is correct?
o: Evenings were noisier, and cats showed more fear then
Mornings were noisier, and cats showed more fear and less maintenance behaviour then, with fear increasing when sound changed from quiet to noisy
Sound had no effect on behaviour, and males showed more fear
mcqs.e: The authors concluded that reducing noise may improve welfare, and cats vary significantly in responsiveness.

title: Animal sheltering: A scoping literature review grounded in institutional ethnography
authors: Koralesky KE, Rankin JM, Fraser D
citation: Koralesky KE, Rankin JM, Fraser D Animal sheltering: A scoping literature review grounded in institutional ethnography. Animal Welfare. 2023. doi:10.1017/awf.2022.4
abstract: The authors examined research on animal sheltering through an institutional ethnography lens, focusing on actual work practices. They reviewed literature on three main areas: shelter staff experiences, animal relinquishment, and length of stay in shelters. Key findings reveal that euthanasia-related stress dominates research on staff, yet focus group participants emphasized decision-making tensions rather than the act itself. Research on relinquishment relies heavily on surveys and database records with significant limitations. Length of stay studies focus on animal characteristics like breed and color, overlooking actual work processes like veterinary treatment and behavioral modification. The authors conclude that institutional ethnography offers valuable insights by examining concrete work activities that current quantitative approaches overlook, potentially leading to better support for both animals and staff.

mcqs.q: A scoping review of animal sheltering research used institutional ethnography. What did it find about research on staff and length of stay?
o: Staff research emphasised euthanasia-related stress, though staff described decision-making tensions, and length of stay studies looked at animal traits and overlooked work processes such as treatment and behaviour modification
Staff research emphasised pay, and length of stay studies emphasised work processes
Both areas used direct observation, so they described actual work practice
mcqs.e: Relinquishment research relied heavily on surveys and database records with significant limitations.

title: Using institutional ethnography to analyse animal sheltering and protection I: Animal protection work
authors: Koralesky KE, Rankin JM, Fraser D
citation: Koralesky KE, Rankin JM, Fraser D Using institutional ethnography to analyse animal sheltering and protection I: Animal protection work. Animal Welfare. 2023. doi:10.1017/awf.2023.39
abstract: Animal protection enforcement in Canada relies on citizens reporting concerns, yet the actual work processes of law enforcement have received minimal scholarly attention. This study employed institutional ethnography to examine the daily activities of call centre operators and animal protection officers. The research revealed that staff attempt to identify evidence of animal 'distress' as legally defined, though many cases—such as animals in isolated or deprived situations—fall short of this definition, preventing intervention. Officers face constraints from privacy and property law requirements, and must document compliance attempts to justify further action including search warrants. These limitations can delay or prevent beneficial intervention. Officers sometimes work creatively to advocate for animals when legal tools prove insufficient. The study recommends expanding the legal definition of distress to better address animals' needs, developing broader intervention options for officers, and conducting ethnographic research across jurisdictions with different legal frameworks to understand how laws and policies organize animal protection work.

mcqs.q: An animal protection officer in Canada finds a dog that is isolated and deprived of stimulation, but there is no clear physical distress. Based on an institutional ethnography of these officers, why is intervention often prevented?
o: Officers are not permitted to respond to citizen reports without a veterinarian's opinion
The case falls short of the legal definition of 'distress', and privacy and property law require documented compliance attempts before a warrant
Officers have no power to advocate for animals, so cases are closed at the call centre
mcqs.e: Staff look for evidence of legally defined distress, many cases of isolation or deprivation do not meet it, and officers must document compliance attempts to justify search warrants.

title: Using institutional ethnography to analyse animal sheltering and protection II: Animal shelter work
authors: Koralesky KE, Rankin JM, Fraser D
citation: Koralesky KE, Rankin JM, Fraser D Using institutional ethnography to analyse animal sheltering and protection II: Animal shelter work. Animal Welfare. 2023. doi:10.1017/awf.2023.83
abstract: The study employed institutional ethnography to examine how frontline shelter staff's daily activities connect to standardized organizational procedures at a large animal protection organization. Staff regularly perform behavioral assessments and review intake documents to guide animal care and inform potential adopters while safeguarding volunteers and the public. However, staff faced significant time constraints and pressure when working with behaviorally challenged animals because their efforts were primarily directed toward facilitating quick adoptions for most animals and preparing for future kennel space demands. Management systems focused on maintaining manageable animal populations based on available resources, reducing shelter duration, and individualized housing. These systems ultimately limited staff's capacity to provide intensive behavioral work for long-stay animals with serious problems. This situation created occupational stress for caregiving staff who felt emotionally invested in these animals' outcomes. The researchers recommend exploring behavioral modification support and expanding foster programs for animals with specialized needs.

mcqs.q: Institutional ethnography of frontline staff at a large animal protection organisation examined how procedures shape work. What did it find about behaviourally challenged, long-stay animals?
o: Staff had abundant time for behaviour modification, and stress was low
Systems aimed at quick adoptions and kennel space limited intensive behavioural work, causing occupational stress for emotionally invested staff
Staff focused on long-stay animals, and adoptions were slowed
mcqs.e: The authors recommend exploring behaviour modification support and expanding foster programmes for animals with specialised needs.

title: Predictors of successful diversion of cats and dogs away from animal shelter intake: Analysis of data from a self-rehoming website
citation: Ly LH, Protopopova A Predictors of successful diversion of cats and dogs away from animal shelter intake: Analysis of data from a self-rehoming website. Animal Welfare. 2023. doi:10.1017/awf.2023.8
abstract: As animals experience distress in animal shelters, leaders call for increased efforts to divert intake of companion animals away from shelters. One novel intake diversion strategy is supported self-rehoming, where owners find new homes for their animals without surrendering to a physical shelter. This study aimed to identify predictors of successful diversion of animals through the AdoptaPet.com 'Rehome' online platform. Data for dogs (n=100,342) and cats (n=48,484) were analysed through logistic regression to assess the association of animaland owner-related factors and outcome. Overall, 87.1% of dogs and 85.7% of cats were successfully diverted from animal shelters, out of which, 37.8% of dogs and 35.3% of cats were kept by their original owner. Multiple animal-related factors predicted increased odds of diversion (e.g. younger, smaller). Dog and cat owners who set a longer rehoming deadline (i.e. >8 weeks) were over twice as likely to keep or adopt out their animal. Dog owners who surrendered for owner-related reasons had increased odds of diversion in comparison to animal behaviour issues. We conclude that online-supported, self-rehoming platforms provide pet owners with an alternative to relinquishment that may reduce the intake of animals to shelters; however, owners with animals that are not preferred by adopters may have to decide whether to keep their animal or relinquish their animal to a shelter or rescue.

mcqs.q: Data on 148,826 animals from a self-rehoming platform (Rehome) were analysed for diversion from shelter intake. Which finding is correct?
o: About 87% of dogs and 86% of cats were diverted, and owners who set longer rehoming deadlines (over 8 weeks) were over twice as likely to keep or rehome the animal
Most animals ended up in shelters anyway
Deadline length did not matter
mcqs.e: Younger and smaller animals had increased odds of diversion.

title: Companion animal adoption and relinquishment during the COVID-19 pandemic: The experiences of animal rescue staff and volunteers
authors: Carroll GA, Reeve C, Torjussen A
citation: Carroll GA, Reeve C, Torjussen A Companion animal adoption and relinquishment during the COVID-19 pandemic: The experiences of animal rescue staff and volunteers. Animal Welfare. 2024. doi:10.1017/awf.2024.15
abstract: There has been a paucity of research into the experiences of animal rescue staff and volunteers during COVID-19. The aim of this qualitative research was to explore the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on companion animal rescue organisations and their staff and volunteers, and to develop a set of recommendations on how to reduce the risk to companion animal welfare during a crisis. Descriptive thematic analysis was used to explore the experiences of staff and volunteers from 28 animal rescue organisations, most of which were based in the UK. Other surveyed countries included Germany, the Republic of Ireland, France, Spain, the USA and Australia. We identify three key themes that reflect the challenges faced by pet rescue organisations during the pandemic: (1) impact on animals; (2) impact on identity; and (3) impact on organisational processes. Key recommendations include the promotion of co-operation and modifications within the sector, the need to understand, and change, detrimental pet-owner behaviours, and the need to clarify the identity of animal rescue organisations within the Government. Both positive and negative outcomes were experienced by animal rescue organisations during the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings should be considered for future crises and indeed the everyday operating procedures of companion animal rescue organisations.

mcqs.q: Staff and volunteers of 28 animal rescue organisations described COVID-19. Which three themes did they identify?
o: Cost of supplies, staff turnover and veterinary access
Increased donations, reduced intake and legislative change
Impact on animals, impact on identity, and impact on organisational processes
mcqs.e: The recommendations include cooperation within the sector, changing detrimental pet-owner behaviours, and clarifying the identity of rescue organisations within Government.

title: Companion animal adoption and relinquishment during the COVID-19 pandemic: Households with children at greatest risk of relinquishing a cat or dog
authors: Carroll GA, Torjussen A, Reeve C
citation: Carroll GA, Torjussen A, Reeve C Companion animal adoption and relinquishment during the COVID-19 pandemic: Households with children at greatest risk of relinquishing a cat or dog. Animal Welfare. 2023. doi:10.1017/awf.2023.77
abstract: The study examined factors linked to pet relinquishment during COVID-19 across multiple countries. Researchers surveyed 3,945 pet owners and identified that households with children were 4.6 times more likely to consider or have already relinquished a cat or dog compared to those without children. Additional risk factors included male pet ownership and younger animal age. Notably, the analysis found no association between online acquisition source and relinquishment risk. Among those who relinquished pets, 76.2% found the decision emotionally difficult, though all agreed it was logically correct. The USA showed significantly higher relinquishment rates than the UK and Italy. The research highlights the need for targeted interventions supporting families with children in pet retention.

mcqs.q: A survey of 3,945 pet owners in several countries examined relinquishment during COVID-19. Which finding is correct?
o: Households with children were 4.6 times more likely to consider or have relinquished a pet, and online acquisition source was not associated with risk
Households without children were most at risk
Online acquisition greatly increased risk
mcqs.e: Most who relinquished found the decision emotionally difficult.

title: Shelter and rescue programmes associated with higher live release and lower return rates for dogs
citation: Reese LA Shelter and rescue programmes associated with higher live release and lower return rates for dogs. Animal Welfare. 2021. doi:10.7120/09627286.30.4.005
abstract: The research examines how shelter characteristics and initiatives affect positive outcomes for dogs. Drawing on survey data from 370 U.S. animal shelters and rescues, the study identifies three key factors associated with improved results: avoiding breed designations for mixed-breed dogs, maintaining robust foster networks, and implementing matching systems. The findings indicate that it is the programmes shelters and rescues implement, not simply their human and financial resources, that are associated with positive outcomes.

mcqs.q: A survey of 370 US shelters and rescues identified programmes associated with higher live release and lower return rates for dogs. Which factors?
o: Only larger budgets and more staff
Longer stray holds only
Avoiding breed designations for mixed-breed dogs, maintaining robust foster networks and implementing matching systems
mcqs.e: It is the programmes, not simply the resources, that are associated with positive outcomes.

title: The role of breed and personality descriptions in influencing perceptions of shelter dog adoptability
authors: Archer C, Hall NJ, Andrukonis A
citation: Archer C, Hall NJ, Andrukonis A The role of breed and personality descriptions in influencing perceptions of shelter dog adoptability. Animal Welfare. 2025. doi:10.1017/awf.2025.10043
abstract: The study examined how breed labels and personality descriptions affect potential adopters' likelihood of choosing shelter dogs. Researchers presented dog photographs to participants under four conditions: photo alone, photo with breed identification, photo with personality traits, and photo with both elements combined. Key findings indicate that descriptions significantly increased perceived adoptability, while breed labels decreased it. Specific breed designations like Chihuahua mix, Chow mix, and Jack Russell Terrier mix negatively influenced adoption interest, whereas 'Lab mix' improved ratings. Personality descriptors such as affectionate, calm, and friendly boosted perceived adoptability; notably, 'energetic' reduced adoption interest. The research suggests removing breed labels and incorporating positive personality descriptions could enhance adoption outcomes and potentially reduce how long dogs remain in shelters, thereby supporting animal welfare objectives.

mcqs.q: Participants viewed dog photographs alone or with breed labels and/or personality descriptions. What was found?
o: Breed labels raised adoptability
Descriptions lowered adoptability
Personality descriptions raised perceived adoptability, breed labels lowered it, and 'energetic' reduced interest while 'affectionate', 'calm' and 'friendly' increased it
mcqs.e: The authors suggest removing breed labels and adding positive personality descriptions.

title: Shelter Worker's Experiences and Perceptions of Capacity for Care (C4C)
authors: Hobson S, Bateman S, Coe JB, Oblak ML
journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science
citation: Hobson S, Bateman S, Coe JB, Oblak ML Shelter Worker's Experiences and Perceptions of Capacity for Care (C4C). Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science. 2023. doi:10.1080/10888705.2021.1910033
abstract: Capacity for Care (C4C) is a shelter population management strategy which utilizes managed intake to optimize in-shelter populations based on housing capacity and available resources. The purpose of this study was to (1) understand staff experiences using managed intake, (2) explore staff perceptions of how the C4C model has been regarded by other staff at their facility, and (3) explore the response of community members who are attempting to relinquish their cats, as perceived by the staff who are communicating with cat owners and scheduling relinquishment. Participants recruited from shelters who practiced C4C participated in a semi-structured interview and completed a written survey to share their experiences and perceptions of C4C. Based on the perceptions of the participants, evidence suggests the waitlist may decrease the admission of owned cats to the shelter as a result of advising cat owners about alternatives to relinquishment. Additional investigation would help clarify how managed intake affects community cats awaiting shelter admission.

mcqs.q: Shelter staff using Capacity for Care (managed intake) were interviewed about its effects. What did their perceptions suggest?
o: The waitlist may reduce admission of owned cats by advising owners on alternatives to relinquishment, but effects on community cats awaiting admission need study
It increased owned cat admissions, and community cats benefited
It had no effect on owners, and staff were opposed to the model
mcqs.e: The model optimises in-shelter populations to housing capacity and resources.

title: Community factors and animal shelter outcomes
journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science
citation: Reese LA Community factors and animal shelter outcomes. Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science. 2024. doi:10.1080/10888705.2022.2063021
abstract: This research explores connections between the nature of a community, the type of animal shelter it has, how animals arrive at the shelter, and outcomes for the animals in terms of adoption or euthanasia. Based on data from Shelter Animals Count, the study concludes that the nature of the local community is related to the type of shelter it is served by, how dogs arrive at the shelter, and directly to outcomes. Areas with greater economic stress and lower educational attainment are more likely to have a municipal shelter, which increases stray intake, and ultimately euthanasia. Community economic stress is also directly associated with lower adoption and higher euthanasia rates. The findings of the study suggest a multi-pronged strategy to increase adoptions and reduce euthanasia focusing on both animal shelters but also using a One Health approach to improve the welfare of both humans and non-human animals.

mcqs.q: A study of Shelter Animals Count data linked community characteristics to shelter outcomes. Which relationship was found?
o: Economically stressed areas had higher adoption rates and lower euthanasia
Areas with greater economic stress and lower education were more likely to have a municipal shelter, with more stray intake, lower adoption and higher euthanasia
Community factors were unrelated to shelter type or outcomes
mcqs.e: The authors suggest a One Health approach improving welfare of people and animals.

title: Attitudes Toward Spay/Neuter in the US Population: Urban/Rural, Cat/Dog, and Demographic Differences
citation: Glasser CL Attitudes Toward Spay/Neuter in the US Population: Urban/Rural, Cat/Dog, and Demographic Differences. Anthrozoös. 2021. doi:10.1080/08927936.2021.1874112
abstract: An online survey of 991 US adults examines differences in attitudes among the general US population toward spaying and neutering cats and dogs, with a focus on differences between urban and rural respondents and the influence of demographic characteristics. Twelve items measure attitudes toward spay/neuter. Each item is analyzed with a separate multiple regression to understand urban–rural, cat–dog and demographic differences in attitudes. Results indicate fewer urban–rural and cat–dog differences than expected, though rural respondents are less likely to find the practice cruel, think animals should have a litter before sterilization, or support laws to require sterilization. People asked about dogs are more likely to agree that spay/neuter operations are expensive but are less likely to believe it is the right thing to do than those asked about cats. The most prevalent characteristics impacting attitudes are guardianship, age, and gender, with guardians more likely to attribute positive health and behavioral outcomes to sterilization and feel that it is morally and socially positive.

mcqs.q: An online survey of 991 US adults compared attitudes toward spay-neuter by urban/rural residence and species. Which finding is correct?
o: Urban and rural attitudes differed completely

There were fewer urban-rural and cat-dog differences than expected, with rural respondents less likely to find the practice cruel or support mandatory laws, and guardianship, age and gender most influential
Dog respondents thought sterilisation was cheap
mcqs.e: Guardians more often attributed positive health and behavioural outcomes to sterilisation.

title: Temporal trends in intake category data for animal shelter and rescue organizations in Colorado from 2008 to 2018
authors: Hawes SM, Hupe TM, Gandenberger J, Morris KN
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
citation: Hawes SM, Hupe TM, Gandenberger J, Morris KN Temporal trends in intake category data for animal shelter and rescue organizations in Colorado from 2008 to 2018. Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association. 2022. doi:10.2460/javma.20.08.0426
abstract: Objective: To investigate trends in animal shelter and rescue organization intake for dogs and cats in Colorado from 2008 to 2018. Sample: 482 animal shelters and rescue organizations that reported annual intake data to the State of Colorado Department of Agriculture for 1,086,630 dogs and 702,333 cats. Procedures: Total intake, intake for each of 5 Pet Animal Care and Facilities Act (PACFA) categories (stray, owner surrender, intrastate transfer, interstate transfer, or other), and community-based intake (total intake after exclusion of transfers) of dogs and cats were assessed in total and for each organization type (shelter or rescue organization). The number taken in per year, number taken in/1,000 capita, and number in each intake category as a percentage of total intake were analyzed with linear regression models. Results: Trend lines indicated that total dog intake increased over the study period, but there was no change when these data were adjusted for the human population. Additionally, cat intake decreased over time according to both of these measures. For dogs, the stray percentage decreased while the interstate transfer percentage increased over time. Cat stray percentages also decreased while owner surrender percentages increased. Rescue organizations showed the largest increase in dog interstate transfers. Conclusions and Clinical Relevance: Monitoring intake category trends at the state level can help guide resource allocation and policy decisions for both shelters and rescue organizations.

mcqs.q: Colorado shelters and rescues reported intake data from 2008 to 2018. Which trend was found?
o: Dog intake per capita rose sharply, and stray percentages increased
Dog intake per capita was unchanged and cat intake decreased, with stray percentages falling and, for dogs, interstate transfers rising
Cat intake rose, and owner surrenders fell
mcqs.e: Rescue organisations showed the largest increase in dog interstate transfers, and monitoring these trends can guide resource allocation.

title: Retrospective review reveals few complications of ovarian pedicle tie in 15,927 cats undergoing ovariohysterectomy at a large HQHVSN clinic and training facility in the United States: 2017–2018
authors: Rigdon-Brestle K, Accornero VH, Amtower M, Slater MR
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
citation: Rigdon-Brestle K, Accornero VH, Amtower M, Slater MR Retrospective review reveals few complications of ovarian pedicle tie in 15,927 cats undergoing ovariohysterectomy at a large HQHVSN clinic and training facility in the United States: 2017–2018. Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association. 2022. doi:10.2460/javma.21.09.0405
abstract: Objective: To determine the rate of complications associated with the ovarian pedicle tie procedure in cats undergoing ovariohysterectomy and to examine whether cat characteristics or surgeon experience level were associated with complications. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Animals: 15,927 cats that underwent ovariohysterectomy with the ovarian pedicle tie procedure at a large high-quality, high-volume spay-neuter (HQHVSN) clinic and training facility in the US between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2018. Procedures: Data were extracted from electronic and paper medical records. Complications examined included pedicle drop or tear, pedicle hemorrhage, and pedicle-related death. Complications were coded by a veterinarian blinded to surgeon experience level. Results: Only 19 of 15,927 (0.12%) cats had pedicle-related hemorrhage, and in all instances, hemorrhage was corrected intraoperatively without serious complication or death. No pedicle-related deaths occurred. Cat reproductive status, body weight, age, and surgeon experience level were not significantly associated with pedicle-related complications. Conclusions and Clinical Relevance: The ovarian pedicle tie is a safe technique for ovariohysterectomy in cats when performed in a HQHVSN setting, with a very low rate of pedicle-related hemorrhage. Surgeon experience level did not significantly affect complication rates, suggesting the technique is learnable across skill levels.

mcqs.q: Complications of the ovarian pedicle tie were reviewed in 15,927 cats at a large HQHVSN clinic. What was found?
o: Haemorrhage was common (10%), and novice surgeons had more complications
Only 0.12% had pedicle-related haemorrhage, all corrected intraoperatively, with no pedicle-related deaths and no association with surgeon experience
Pedicle-related deaths were frequent
mcqs.e: Reproductive status, body weight and age were not significantly associated with complications.

title: Daily gabapentin improved behavior modification progress and decreased stress in shelter cats from hoarding environments in a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial
authors: Eagan BH, van Haaften K, Protopopova A
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
citation: Eagan BH, van Haaften K, Protopopova A Daily gabapentin improved behavior modification progress and decreased stress in shelter cats from hoarding environments in a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial. Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association. 2023. doi:10.2460/javma.23.01.0044
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the impact of daily gabapentin on behavior modification progression and signs of stress in fearful shelter cats from hoarding environments. Design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial. Animals: 37 cats from hoarding environments (32 met inclusion criteria). Procedures: Healthy fearful cats were entered into either a gabapentin (10 mg/kg PO q12h) or placebo group upon intake. Both groups received daily behavior modification. Daily measures of cat stress score, latency to emerge from hiding, general in-shelter behavior, and urine suppression were collected. Cats were deemed to have graduated from the program when they met behavioral criteria for adoption or upon shelter departure. Results: Of 32 fearful cats, 28 (87.5%) graduated from the behavior modification program in a median of 11 days (range, 4 to 51 days). Animals receiving gabapentin showed greater behavioral improvement over time compared to those given a placebo, including faster progression through the behavior modification program and lower stress scores. Conclusions and Clinical Relevance: Daily gabapentin can improve behavior modification success and reduce stress in fearful shelter cats from hoarding environments. This finding supports the use of gabapentin as an adjunct to behavior modification programs for difficult-to-adopt cats.

mcqs.q: A healthy, fearful cat from a hoarding environment starts a daily behaviour modification programme. In a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, what was the effect of adding gabapentin at 10 mg/kg by mouth every 12 hours?
o: Lower stress scores but no faster progression through the programme
Faster progression through the programme and lower stress scores than placebo
No difference from placebo, because behaviour modification was the only active factor
mcqs.e: Cats given gabapentin showed greater behavioural improvement over time, including faster progression and lower stress scores. Most cats (87.5%) graduated in a median of 11 days.

title: Vasectomy and ovary-sparing spay in dogs: comparison of health and behavior outcomes with gonadectomized and sexually intact dogs
authors: Zink C, Delgado MM, Stella JL
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
citation: Zink C, Delgado MM, Stella JL Vasectomy and ovary-sparing spay in dogs: comparison of health and behavior outcomes with gonadectomized and sexually intact dogs. Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association. 2023. doi:10.2460/javma.22.08.0382
abstract: Objective: To compare health and behavioral outcomes for dogs that underwent vasectomy or ovary-sparing spay (hysterectomy) with sexually intact dogs or dogs that had undergone traditional castration or ovariohysterectomy. Design: Cross-sectional, web-based survey study. Sample: 6,018 dog owners who responded to a web-based survey between November 3, 2021, and January 7, 2022, providing valid surveys for 6,018 dogs including 1,056 sexually intact, 1,672 castrated, and 58 vasectomized male dogs and 792 sexually intact, 2,281 spayed, and 159 ovary-sparing spayed female dogs. Procedures: Owners were asked questions about orthopedic and other health problems, cancer, and problematic behavior. Results: Longer exposure to gonadal hormones, regardless of reproductive status, was associated with reduced odds of general health problems and both problematic and nuisance behaviors. No significant differences in health outcomes were identified between dogs that had undergone vasectomy versus those that were castrated, or between ovary-sparing spay and traditional spay. However, gonadectomized dogs had higher odds of orthopedic problems compared to sexually intact dogs and those retaining gonads. Conclusions and Clinical Relevance: This study, the first to compare outcomes across all five reproductive statuses, suggests gonadal hormone exposure — regardless of reproductive status — is protective for overall health and behavior. Individualized reproductive surgery decisions should consider the potential health implications of complete gonadectomy.

mcqs.q: A survey of 6,018 dog owners compared vasectomy and ovary-sparing spay with traditional gonadectomy and intact dogs. Which finding is correct?
o: Vasectomised dogs had much higher orthopaedic problems than castrated dogs
Longer exposure to gonadal hormones was associated with fewer general health and behaviour problems, and vasectomy and ovary-sparing spay showed no health differences from castration and spay
Gonadectomised dogs had lower orthopaedic problem odds
mcqs.e: Gonadectomised dogs had higher odds of orthopaedic problems than intact dogs and dogs retaining gonads.

title: Natural history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats from rehoming centers: The CatScan II study
authors: Novo Matos J, Payne JR, Seo J, Luis Fuentes V
citation: Novo Matos J, Payne JR, Seo J, Luis Fuentes V Natural history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats from rehoming centers: The CatScan II study. Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine. 2022. doi:10.1111/jvim.16576
abstract: Background: The natural history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) in cats has been mainly studied in cats referred for suspected heart disease. Few data are available on factors associated with development of HCM in cats without clinical signs at baseline. Objectives: To characterize the natural history of HCM in cats from rehoming centers and identify echocardiographic variables associated with HCM development. Animals: One hundred seven cats from UK rehoming centers without a history of clinical signs of cardiac or systemic disease at the time of adoption. Methods: Prospective longitudinal study. After rehoming, cats were reexamined with serial echocardiography over a median follow-up of 5.6 years. Results: At baseline, 68 cats were echocardiographically normal, 18 were equivocal, and 21 had HCM. Nineteen additional cats developed HCM during follow-up. Lower left atrial fractional shortening, higher left ventricular fractional shortening, and higher body weight at baseline predicted HCM development. Cardiovascular events occurred in 21% of cats with HCM. Conclusions and Clinical Relevance: Lower left atrial systolic function appears to precede overt HCM in cats from rehoming centers. The prevalence of HCM in this unselected population was substantial, and cardiovascular events occurred in a meaningful proportion of affected cats, highlighting the importance of cardiac screening in shelter and rehoming populations.

mcqs.q: One hundred seven cats from UK rehoming centres were followed with serial echocardiography for a median of 5.6 years. What was found?
o: No cat developed cardiomyopathy
Only cats with clinical signs at baseline were affected
Nineteen additional cats developed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, predicted by lower left atrial fractional shortening, higher left ventricular fractional shortening and higher body weight
mcqs.e: Cardiovascular events occurred in 21% of cats with the disease.

title: Renal amyloid-A amyloidosis in cats: Characterization of proteinuria and biomarker discovery, and associations with kidney histology
authors: Palizzotto C, Ferri F, Callegari C, Rossi F, Manfredi M, Carcangiu L, Gerardi G, Ferro S, Cavicchioli L, Müller E, Weiss M, Vogt AC, Lavatelli F, Ricagno S, Hurley K, Zini E
citation: Palizzotto C, Ferri F, Callegari C, Rossi F, Manfredi M, Carcangiu L, Gerardi G, Ferro S, Cavicchioli L, Müller E, Weiss M, Vogt AC, Lavatelli F, Ricagno S, Hurley K, Zini E Renal amyloid-A amyloidosis in cats: Characterization of proteinuria and biomarker discovery, and associations with kidney histology. Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine. 2024. doi:10.1111/jvim.16920
abstract: Background: Systemic AA amyloidosis recently was shown to have a high prevalence in shelter cats in Italy and was associated with azotemia and proteinuria. Objectives: To investigate urine protein profiles and identify diagnostic biomarkers in cats with renal AA amyloidosis. Animals: Twenty-nine shelter cats. Methods: Case-control study. Cats with renal proteinuria that died or were euthanized between 2018 and 2021 were included. Histology was used to characterize renal damage; immunohistochemistry confirmed AA amyloidosis. Urine protein-to-creatinine (UPC) and urine amyloid A-to-creatinine (UAAC) ratios were calculated. Urine protein profiling was done using sodium dodecyl sulfate-agarose gel electrophoresis (SDS-AGE) and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Results: Nineteen cats had AA amyloidosis. Affected cats had higher UPC and UAAC ratios than unaffected cats. Mixed proteinuria was identified in 89.4% of affected cats. LC-MS identified 63 potential biomarkers; urine apolipoprotein C-III was higher in cats with AA amyloidosis. AA amyloidosis was associated with glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis. Conclusions and Clinical Relevance: Renal AA amyloidosis in shelter cats is associated with mixed proteinuria, specific kidney lesions, and elevated urine biomarkers. Urine apolipoprotein C-III may assist in diagnosis. Further research is needed regarding the role of lipid transport proteins in this condition.

mcqs.q: Twenty-nine shelter cats with renal proteinuria were investigated for AA amyloidosis. Which urinary finding was more frequent in affected cats?
o: Purely tubular proteinuria and lower UPC
Normal urine protein profiles in most cats
Mixed proteinuria, higher UPC and urine amyloid A-to-creatinine ratios, and higher urine apolipoprotein C-III
mcqs.e: Nineteen cats had AA amyloidosis, associated with glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis.

title: Feline panleukopenia virus DNA shedding following modified live virus vaccination in a shelter setting
authors: Jacobson LS, Janke KJ, Ha K, Giacinti JA, Weese JS
citation: Jacobson LS, Janke KJ, Ha K, Giacinti JA, Weese JS Feline panleukopenia virus DNA shedding following modified live virus vaccination in a shelter setting. The Veterinary Journal. 2022. doi:10.1016/j.tvjl.2021.105783
abstract: This study assessed the frequency and timing of feline panleukopenia virus (FPV) DNA shedding in feces following administration of a modified live FPV vaccine in a shelter setting. Feces were collected from 37 shelter cats that did not meet clinical criteria for panleukopenia on the day of vaccination (day 0) or on days 3, 7, 14, and 21 post-vaccination. A commercial quantitative PCR (qPCR) fecal pathogen panel and a canine parvovirus point-of-care antigen test were performed on each sample. Positive qPCR results were obtained from 8/37 cats (21.6%) without clinical signs, primarily on day 7. DNA copy numbers were substantially lower following vaccination than in clinically infected cats. The point-of-care antigen test was negative in all vaccinated cats. FPV qPCR cannot differentiate subclinical infection from vaccine virus shedding. The authors recommend limiting PCR testing to cats with strong clinical suspicion of panleukopenia and considering recent vaccination timing when interpreting results, to avoid unnecessary outbreak responses based on false-positive PCR results in vaccinated shelter cats.

mcqs.q: Shelter cats were tested for faecal FPV DNA after modified live vaccination. What was found and recommended?
o: No vaccinated cat had positive qPCR, so results are always reliable
About 22% of clinically well cats had positive qPCR, mostly on day 7, with low copy numbers and negative antigen tests, so test only cats with strong clinical suspicion and consider vaccine timing
All vaccinated cats had positive antigen tests, so isolation is required
mcqs.e: FPV qPCR cannot differentiate subclinical infection from vaccine virus shedding.

title: Identification of spayed and neutered cats and dogs: Veterinary training and compliance with practice guidelines
authors: Mielo MR, Amirian ES, Levy JK
citation: Mielo MR, Amirian ES, Levy JK Identification of spayed and neutered cats and dogs: Veterinary training and compliance with practice guidelines. The Veterinary Journal. 2022. doi:10.1016/j.tvjl.2022.105856
abstract: Spay/neuter identification tattoos and ear-tipping are simple, cost-effective methods to minimize unnecessary anesthesia and surgery in companion animals, or the misidentification of sexually intact animals. This study assessed training of sterilization identifiers in US and Canadian veterinary schools and practitioner compliance with guidelines for identifiers via surveys conducted in 2019. Faculty in all 34 participating veterinary schools reported curricula included sterilization identifiers in 31% of lecture-based training, 75% of spay/neuter laboratory-based training, and 38% of clinical practice-based training. A total of 425 facilities performing spay/neuter reported frequency and technical aspects of sterilization identifiers. Facilities encountering large numbers of animals of unknown background, performing a high number of surgeries, or with specialized spay/neuter training were significantly more likely to use identifiers. Only 5% of private practices tattooed all owned animals and 21% tattooed all unowned animals. In contrast, 80% of shelters and 72% of spay/neuter clinics tattooed animals. Green tattoos placed near surgical incisions represented the predominant technique. Enhanced training and broader implementation of sterilization identification best practices are essential to prevent unnecessary surgeries and unintended breeding in animals misidentified as sexually intact.

mcqs.q: Surveys assessed use of sterilisation identifiers (tattoo, ear tip) by veterinary schools and 425 facilities. Which finding is correct?
o: Only 5% of private practices tattooed all owned animals, while 80% of shelters and most spay-neuter clinics used identifiers
Most private practices tattooed all animals
Shelters rarely used identifiers
mcqs.e: Identifiers minimise unnecessary anaesthesia and surgery.

title: Capturing free-roaming dogs for sterilisation: A multi-site study in Goa, India
authors: Fielding HR, Fernandes KA, Amulya VR, Belgayer D, Misquita A, Kenny R, Gibson AD, Gamble L, Bronsvoort BMdC, Mellanby RJ, Mazeri S
citation: Fielding HR, Fernandes KA, Amulya VR, Belgayer D, Misquita A, Kenny R, Gibson AD, Gamble L, Bronsvoort BMdC, Mellanby RJ, Mazeri S Capturing free-roaming dogs for sterilisation: A multi-site study in Goa, India. Preventive Veterinary Medicine. 2023. doi:10.1016/j.prevetmed.2023.105996
abstract: Street and free-roaming dog populations in lowand middle-income countries pose public health risks including rabies transmission. Surgical sterilisation campaigns are a key component of humane dog population management. This multi-site study documented dog capture rates across six sterilization campaigns in Goa, India, using spatial coordinates and population surveys to assess campaign efficiency. Results demonstrate that as sterilization coverage increases within a community, capturing remaining intact dogs becomes progressively more difficult, with corresponding escalation in unit costs per dog captured. The study quantified diminishing returns on capture efficiency as the proportion of sterilized animals rises. These findings have important implications for planning efficient, cost-effective dog population management interventions: targeting areas of lower coverage first and adapting capture strategies as coverage improves may maximize program impact. Understanding capture dynamics is essential for sustainable free-roaming dog population control programs.

mcqs.q: Capture rates of free-roaming dogs were documented across six sterilisation campaigns in Goa. What was found?
o: Capture became easier as coverage rose
As sterilisation coverage rose, capturing remaining intact dogs became harder and unit costs rose, showing diminishing returns
Costs did not change
mcqs.e: Targeting lower-coverage areas first may maximise impact.

title: Frequency of SARS-CoV-2 infection in dogs and cats: Results of a retrospective serological survey in Šumadija District, Serbia
authors: Stanojevic S, Radojicic S, Misic D, Srejic D, Vasiljevic DV, Prokic K, Ilic N
citation: Stanojevic S, Radojicic S, Misic D, Srejic D, Vasiljevic DV, Prokic K, Ilic N Frequency of SARS-CoV-2 infection in dogs and cats: Results of a retrospective serological survey in Šumadija District, Serbia. Preventive Veterinary Medicine. 2022. doi:10.1016/j.prevetmed.2022.105755
abstract: This retrospective serosurvey examined SARS-CoV-2 exposure in companion and stray animals in Šumadija District, Serbia, during the COVID-19 pandemic. A total of samples from dogs and cats were tested using a neutralization assay. The relative frequency of SARS-CoV-2 infection in dogs was 1.45% and in cats was 5.56%. Pet owner seropositivity was 11%, and seropositivity in pets with close owner contact was 9%. Stray animals showed lower seroprevalence compared to household pets. The results confirm that companion dogs and cats are susceptible to SARS-CoV-2, with cats showing higher seroprevalence than dogs. Human-to-pet transmission was identified as the primary infection route. Findings emphasize the importance of One Health surveillance including companion and stray animals during respiratory virus pandemics.

mcqs.q: A serosurvey of companion and stray animals in Šumadija District, Serbia, found which pattern?
o: Dogs had higher seroprevalence than cats, and pets infected their owners
Stray animals had higher seroprevalence than pets
Cats had higher seroprevalence than dogs (5.56% vs 1.45%), stray animals lower than household pets, and human-to-pet transmission was the primary route
mcqs.e: Owner seropositivity was 11%, and the authors emphasise One Health surveillance.

title: Top-down animal welfare crisis communication during the COVID-19 pandemic: Animal care worker information sources, self-perceived knowledge and welfare concerns
authors: Miller SL, Kwan JX, Dalton KR, Waite KB, Davis MF
citation: Miller SL, Kwan JX, Dalton KR, Waite KB, Davis MF Top-down animal welfare crisis communication during the COVID-19 pandemic: Animal care worker information sources, self-perceived knowledge and welfare concerns. The Veterinary Record. 2025. doi:10.1002/vetr.5498
abstract: This cross-sectional study assessed animal care worker responses to identify factors valuable for crisis preparedness planning during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants included small animal veterinary workers (n = 1,209) and shelter/rescue workers (n = 132). Shelter and rescue workers (SRC workers) more often reported frequent communication from their organization, self-perceived expert knowledge, and having welfare concerns related to the pandemic compared to veterinary workers. Information sources differed significantly by worker type, with SRC workers relying more heavily on organizational communications. The study highlights a potential need for increased, more harmonized crisis communication from leading public and animal health entities to better support both veterinary and shelter worker populations. Differences in crisis communication patterns between private practice and shelter workers may affect their ability to implement appropriate biosecurity and animal welfare measures during future public health emergencies.

mcqs.q: A survey of 1,209 veterinary workers and 132 shelter and rescue workers examined COVID-19 communication. Which finding is correct?
o: Veterinary workers relied more on organisational communication
There were no differences between groups
Shelter and rescue workers more often reported frequent organisational communication, self-perceived expert knowledge and welfare concerns, and relied more on organisational sources
mcqs.e: The authors suggest more harmonised crisis communication.

title: How do accessible veterinary care providers evaluate programmes and engage communities? Results of a qualitative analysis of Canadian service providers
authors: Rausch Q, Geddes N, Liao TP, Van Patter L
citation: Rausch Q, Geddes N, Liao TP, Van Patter L How do accessible veterinary care providers evaluate programmes and engage communities? Results of a qualitative analysis of Canadian service providers. The Veterinary Record. 2026. doi:10.1002/vetr.6022
abstract: Accessible veterinary care (AVC) programmes aim to reduce barriers to veterinary services for under-resourced pet owners and communities. This qualitative study examined 18 Canadian accessible veterinary care providers through focus groups and interviews to understand how they evaluate their programmes and engage with communities. Analysis revealed large diversity in programme initiation, evolution, and evaluation approaches. Concerns identified included ethical challenges around community engagement, funder reporting requirements creating administrative burden, and limited knowledge and resources for rigorous programme evaluation. Providers highlighted the need for standardized metrics and evaluation frameworks to demonstrate programme impact. The study underscores the importance of community-centred, culturally appropriate service delivery and the need for better infrastructure to support AVC provider capacity for evaluation and long-term programme sustainability.

mcqs.q: Eighteen Canadian accessible veterinary care providers were interviewed about evaluation and community engagement. Which concerns emerged?
o: Excess funding and no need for evaluation
Ethical challenges in engagement, administrative burden from funder reporting, and limited knowledge and resources for rigorous evaluation
Excessive standardisation
mcqs.e: Providers called for standardised metrics and evaluation frameworks.

title: Shelter dogs as reservoirs of international clones of Escherichia coli carrying mcr-1.1 and bla(CTX-M) resistance genes in Lima, Peru
authors: Ayzanoa B, Salvatierra G, Cuicapuza D, Furlan JPR, Sellera FP, Chavez L, Esposito F, Tsukayama P, Lincopan N
citation: Ayzanoa B, Salvatierra G, Cuicapuza D, Furlan JPR, Sellera FP, Chavez L, Esposito F, Tsukayama P, Lincopan N Shelter dogs as reservoirs of international clones of Escherichia coli carrying mcr-1.1 and bla(CTX-M) resistance genes in Lima, Peru. Veterinary Microbiology. 2025. doi:10.1016/j.vetmic.2025.110543
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical public health threat worldwide, particularly at the human-animal interface where cross-transmission of critical priority Enterobacterales, such as Escherichia coli, have become increasingly reported. Worryingly, E. coli encoding extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) has been documented in companion animals worldwide. Conversely, the presence of mcr genes, which confer resistance to polymyxins, in bacteria from pets remains more infrequent. In this study, we sequenced and reported on the first genomic data of E. coli strains carrying mcr-1 and/or blaCTX-M genes isolated from rectal swabs of stray dogs in a shelter in the city of Lima, Peru. Antimicrobial susceptibility revealed that E. coli strains exhibited a multidrug resistance profile. In addition to mcr-1 and blaCTX-M genes, other clinically relevant resistance determinants were identified, with notably presence of blaTEM-176 and the novel blaSCO-2 variant. The association of mcr-1.1 and IncI2 plasmid was confirmed. Several virulence genes were detected, classifying strains as putative extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli. Multilocus sequence typing prediction recognized diverse sequence types (ST), including ST155, ST189, ST657, ST746, ST1140, ST3014, and ST7188. This study represents the first report of mcr-positive E. coli in dogs from Peru, emphasizing the need for continuous surveillance and genomic characterization to better understand the transmission dynamics of these critical resistance genes at the human-animal interface. Furthermore, our results provide evidence that stray, and shelter dogs could be a reservoir for the spread of WHO priority pathogens, and/or polymyxin and β-lactam resistance genes, which is a public health and One Health concern that requires appropriate management strategies.

mcqs.q: Rectal swabs from stray dogs in a Lima shelter grew Escherichia coli carrying mcr-1.1 (polymyxin resistance) and blaCTX-M genes, with mcr-1.1 linked to an IncI2 plasmid. What is the most important implication?
o: The dogs pose no AMR risk, because the strains were not carried by humans
Shelter dogs may be reservoirs of WHO priority resistant pathogens, so continued surveillance and genomic characterisation are warranted
Polymyxins are safe to use as prophylaxis in shelter dogs, because resistance is rare
mcqs.e: This was the first report of mcr-positive E. coli in dogs from Peru, and the strains were multidrug resistant and classified as putative extraintestinal pathogens.

title: Streptococcus zooepidemicus in dogs: Exploring a canine pathogen through multilocus sequence typing
authors: Mangano ER, Jones GMC, Suarez-Bonnet A, Waller AS, Priestnall SL
citation: Mangano ER, Jones GMC, Suarez-Bonnet A, Waller AS, Priestnall SL Streptococcus zooepidemicus in dogs: Exploring a canine pathogen through multilocus sequence typing. Veterinary Microbiology. 2024. doi:10.1016/j.vetmic.2024.110059
abstract: Streptococcus equi. subsp. zooepidemicus (S. zooepidemicus) associated diseases in dogs have emerged as a significant concern over recent decades. S. zooepidemicus occurs sporadically in dog populations globally, with increased prevalence in shelters/kennels. This study used multilocus sequence typing (MLST) of 149 independent canine S. zooepidemicus isolates to assess associations between sequence type and breed, country of origin, disease severity, sampling type, year, and behaviour within an outbreak. No clear associations for breed, country, sampling type and year were determined in this study. ST-10 and 123 strains were present within all disease categories, from no clinical signs to severe disease. Assessment of S. zooepidemicus infection in 3 UK outbreaks at the same location found ST-10, 18, 123 strains, and a ST-173 strain in a US outbreak, were associated with haemorrhagic pneumonia and persisted in kennelled populations over time. The ST-173 clonal complex has been noted to have severe virulence capabilities in dogs and other species. S. zooepidemicus seems to thrive in environments with a high risk of transmissibility, overcrowding, stress and naïve populations, particularly for those in shelters/kennels. MLST alone cannot determine the virulence phenotype of S. zooepidemicus in dogs. However, a level of conservancy and diversity within ST allelic loci aids the opportunity to cause severe disease in dogs. Thus, further research into whole genome sequencing and characterising the virulence factors of S. zooepidemicus is warranted in dogs.

mcqs.q: Multilocus sequence typing of 149 canine Streptococcus zooepidemicus isolates found what?
o: Strong associations with breed and country
All strains were harmless to dogs
No clear link to breed, country, sampling type or year, and certain sequence types (such as ST-10, ST-123 and ST-173) were associated with haemorrhagic pneumonia and persisted in kennels
mcqs.e: The organism thrives with overcrowding, stress and naive populations.

title: Canine parvovirus is shed infrequently by cats without diarrhoea in multi-cat environments
authors: Carrai M, Decaro N, Van Brussel K, Dall'Ara P, Desario C, Fracasso M, Šlapeta J, Colombo E, Bo S, Beatty JA, Meers J, Barrs VR
citation: Carrai M, Decaro N, Van Brussel K, Dall'Ara P, Desario C, Fracasso M, Šlapeta J, Colombo E, Bo S, Beatty JA, Meers J, Barrs VR Canine parvovirus is shed infrequently by cats without diarrhoea in multi-cat environments. Veterinary Microbiology. 2021. doi:10.1016/j.vetmic.2021.109204
abstract: Whether subclinical shedding of canine parvovirus (CPV) by cats might contribute to the epidemiology of canine CPV infections, particularly in facilities housing both cats and dogs, requires clarification. Conflicting results are reported to date. Using conventional PCR (cPCR) to amplify the VP2 gene, shedding of the CPV variants (CPV-2a, 2b, 2c) by healthy cats in multi-cat environments was reportedly common in Europe but rare in Australia. The aim of this study was to determine whether low-level faecal CPV shedding occurs in multi-cat environments in Australia and Italy using a TaqMan real-time PCR to detect Carnivore protoparvovirus 1 (CPV and feline parvovirus, FPV) DNA, and minor-groove binder probe real-time PCR assay to differentiate FPV and CPV types and to characterize CPV variants. In total, 741 non-diarrhoeic faecal samples from shelters in Australia (n = 263) and from shelters or cat colonies in Italy (n = 478) were tested. Overall, Carnivore protoparvovirus 1 DNA was detected in 49 of 741 (6.61%) samples. Differentiation was possible for 31 positive samples. FPV was most common among positive samples (28/31, 90.3%). CPV was detected in 4/31 samples (12.9%) including CPV-2a in one sample, CPV-2b in another and co-infections of FPV/CPV-2b and CPV-2a/CPV-2b in the remaining two samples. A high rate of subclinical FPV infection was detected in one shelter during an outbreak of feline panleukopenia, during which 21 of 22 asymptomatic cats (95.5%) sampled were shedding FPV. Faecal shedding of CPV by cats in multi-cat environments is uncommon suggesting that domestic cats are not significant reservoirs of CPV.

mcqs.q: Faecal samples of 741 non-diarrhoeic cats in Australia and Italy were tested for parvovirus DNA. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Carnivore protoparvovirus 1 DNA was found in 6.61%, mostly feline panleukopenia virus, and CPV shedding was uncommon, so cats are not significant CPV reservoirs
Most healthy cats shed CPV, so cats are the main reservoir
No cat shed any parvovirus
mcqs.e: In a panleukopenia outbreak 21 of 22 asymptomatic cats were shedding FPV.

title: Isolation and characterization of Chlamydia felis and its pathogenesis in cats
authors: Chen J, Long J, Zhou H, Huang C, Zhu Y, Wang R, Zhang H, Qin Y, Ouyang K, Wei Z, Huang W, Chen Y
citation: Chen J, Long J, Zhou H, Huang C, Zhu Y, Wang R, Zhang H, Qin Y, Ouyang K, Wei Z, Huang W, Chen Y Isolation and characterization of Chlamydia felis and its pathogenesis in cats. Veterinary Microbiology. 2024. doi:10.1016/j.vetmic.2024.110128
abstract: Feline upper respiratory tract disease (URTD) is a common but complicated disease that occurs in domestic cats, worldwide. 396 cats in Guangxi Province, China were screened for URTD-associated pathogens from March 2022 to August 2023. Mycoplasma felis was found to be the most prevalent infectious agent with a positivity rate of 24.75%, followed by feline calicivirus (FCV), Chlamydia felis, feline herpesvirus 1 (FHV-1) and feline influenza A virus (FeIAV) with rates of 15.91, 11.62, 5.56 and 1.52%, respectively. In particular, C. felis and M. felis were found in 13 of 55 co-infected cats. Of the 46 C. felis-positive samples, one strain, named as GXNN36, was successfully isolated using chicken embryos and it was characterized both in vivo and in vitro. For the cat studies, both highand low-dose challenged groups showed severe conjunctivitis, accompanied by transient fever and respiratory symptoms. C. felis replicated well in turbinate, trachea and lung tissues with high copy numbers and the infection subsequently spread to the livers, spleens, pancreas, kidneys, hearts and intestines. These findings will help our understanding of the role of C. felis in feline URTD and provide a valuable model to evaluate the efficacy of vaccines and therapeutic remedies in the future.

mcqs.q: In a survey of 396 cats in Guangxi with respiratory disease, which was the most prevalent agent, and what did Chlamydia felis challenge cause?
o: Feline herpesvirus 1 (24.75%); no signs at all
Feline influenza A virus (24.75%); only pneumonia
Mycoplasma felis (24.75%); severe conjunctivitis with transient fever and respiratory signs, with spread to other organs
mcqs.e: C. felis and M. felis were found together in 13 of 55 co-infected cats.

title: Feline leukemia virus in owned cats in Southeast Asia and Taiwan
authors: Capozza P, Lorusso E, Colella V, Thibault JC, Tan DY, Tronel JP, Halos L, Beugnet F, Elia G, Nguyen VL, Occhiogrosso L, Martella V, Otranto D, Decaro N
citation: Capozza P, Lorusso E, Colella V, Thibault JC, Tan DY, Tronel JP, Halos L, Beugnet F, Elia G, Nguyen VL, Occhiogrosso L, Martella V, Otranto D, Decaro N Feline leukemia virus in owned cats in Southeast Asia and Taiwan. Veterinary Microbiology. 2021. doi:10.1016/j.vetmic.2021.109008
abstract: Feline leukaemia virus (FeLV) is a retrovirus associated with fatal disease in cats with infection in its progressive form. The researchers assessed FeLV circulation across Southeast Asian countries and Taiwan during 2017–2018 using ELISA and nested PCR testing. Of 47 FeLV-positive cats, 32 were confirmed positive through molecular testing. Detection rates varied significantly by location, with frequency of occurrence of FeLV proviral DNA ranging from 0% (0/43 positive samples) in Indonesia to 18.5% (22/119 positive samples) in Thailand. Statistical analysis revealed associations between FeLV positivity and country origin, age, lifestyle, and oral mucosal abnormalities. The authors conclude that additional research is necessary to better understand FeLV distribution patterns across the region.

mcqs.q: FeLV was tested by ELISA and nested PCR in owned cats in Southeast Asia and Taiwan. Which finding is correct?
o: Detection varied by country (0% in Indonesia to 18.5% in Thailand) and was associated with age, lifestyle and oral mucosal abnormalities
Detection was identical in all countries
FeLV was found only in Taiwan
mcqs.e: Thirty-two of 47 ELISA-positive cats were confirmed by molecular testing.

title: Seroprevalence and risk factors for Toxoplasma gondii exposure in Australian feral and stray cats using an in-house modified agglutination test
authors: Liyanage KLDTD, Amery-Gale J, Uboldi AD, Adriaanse K, Firestone SM, Tonkin CJ, Jabbar A, Hufschmid J
citation: Liyanage KLDTD, Amery-Gale J, Uboldi AD, Adriaanse K, Firestone SM, Tonkin CJ, Jabbar A, Hufschmid J Seroprevalence and risk factors for Toxoplasma gondii exposure in Australian feral and stray cats using an in-house modified agglutination test. Veterinary Parasitology. 2024. doi:10.1016/j.vetpar.2024.110306
abstract: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally distributed zoonotic protist, capable of infecting all warm-blooded animals. In Australia, cats (Felis catus) are the only definitive host capable of spreading T. gondii infection via oocysts. Free-roaming cats are widespread in Australia and can play a central role in the ecology of T. gondii. Therefore, understanding the epidemiology of this parasite in stray and feral cats is essential to understanding the potential risk of infection in animals and humans. Due to a lack of easily accessible commercial kits, an in-house modified agglutination test (MAT) was established to test for IgG antibodies against T. gondii, using cell culture-derived T. gondii tachyzoites, and compared with a commercial MAT. A total of 552 serum samples collected during 2018–2021 from stray (n = 456) and feral cats (n = 90) (samples with missing data n = 6) from four Australian states, representing different age groups of both sexes, were screened for antibodies against T. gondii. Risk factors for T. gondii infection were assessed using multivariable logistic regression analysis. The in-house MAT had excellent agreement with the commercial MAT and provided a reliable and economical serological tool for T. gondii screening in animals. The overall observed seroprevalence for T. gondii in cats was 40.4% (223/552). Bodyweight (as a proxy for age), geographical location, season and whether cats were feral or stray, were factors associated with T. gondii seropositivity in cats. Sex was not found to be a risk factor for T. gondii infection in feral and stray cats. This study shows that Australian stray and feral cats have a high T. gondii seroprevalence, which may translate to significant health impacts for wildlife species, livestock and the public.

mcqs.q: A modified agglutination test (MAT) for Toxoplasma gondii antibodies was tested on 552 stray and feral cats in Australia. What did the study conclude?
o: The in-house MAT disagreed with the commercial test, and seroprevalence was low
The in-house MAT agreed well with a commercial MAT and is a reliable, economical tool, and stray and feral cats had high seroprevalence, with sex not a risk factor
Male cats had a much higher risk than females, and dogs were the definitive hosts
mcqs.e: Cats are the only definitive host in Australia, so free-roaming cats play a central role in the ecology of the parasite.

title: Renal alterations in cats (Felis catus) housed in shelters and affected by systemic AA-amyloidosis: Clinicopathological data, histopathology, and ultrastructural features
authors: Ferri F, Ferro S, Benali SL, Aresu L, Muscardin L, Porporato F, Rossi F, Guglielmetti C, Gallo E, Palizzotto C, Callegari C, Ricagno S, Mazza M, Coppola LM, Gerardi G, Lavatelli F, Caminito S, Mazzini G, Palladini G, Merlini G, Zini E
citation: Ferri F, Ferro S, Benali SL, Aresu L, Muscardin L, Porporato F, Rossi F, Guglielmetti C, Gallo E, Palizzotto C, Callegari C, Ricagno S, Mazza M, Coppola LM, Gerardi G, Lavatelli F, Caminito S, Mazzini G, Palladini G, Merlini G, Zini E Renal alterations in cats (Felis catus) housed in shelters and affected by systemic AA-amyloidosis: Clinicopathological data, histopathology, and ultrastructural features. Veterinary Pathology. 2024. doi:10.1177/03009858241257903
abstract: AA-amyloidosis is frequent in shelter cats, and chronic kidney disease is the foremost cause of death. The aims were to describe kidney laboratory and microscopic findings in shelter cats with AA-amyloidosis. Cats were included if kidney specimens were collected post-mortem and laboratory data were available within 6 months before death. Renal lesions were evaluated with optical and electron microscopy. Mass spectrometry was used to characterize amyloid. Nine domestic short-hair cats were included; 4 females and 5 males with a median age of 8 years (range = 2–13). All cats had blood analyses and urinalyses available. Serum creatinine concentrations were increased in 6 cats and symmetric dimethylarginine was increased in all of the cats. All of the cats had proteinuria. Eight of 9 cats had amyloid in the medulla, and 9 had amyloid in the cortex (glomeruli). All cats had amyloid in the interstitium. Six cats had concurrent interstitial nephritis and 1 had membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis. All cats had extrarenal amyloid deposits. Amyloid was AA in each case. Mass spectrometry confirmed amyloid was AA in each case. In conclusion, renal deposition of amyloid occurs in both cortex and medulla in shelter cats and is associated with azotemia and proteinuria. Renal involvement of systemic AA-amyloidosis should be considered in shelter cats with chronic kidney disease. The cat represents a natural model of renal AA-amyloidosis.

mcqs.q: Nine shelter cats with systemic AA amyloidosis had kidney tissue examined. Which finding is correct?
o: Amyloid was in the cortex (glomeruli) and medulla, all had proteinuria and increased symmetric dimethylarginine, and renal involvement should be considered in shelter cats with chronic kidney disease
Amyloid was confined to the medulla, and creatinine was normal in all cats
Amyloid was AL type, and extrarenal deposits were absent
mcqs.e: Mass spectrometry confirmed AA type in every case.

title: Serial examination of the pancreas from shelter cats euthanized for population control for the prevalence of histologic and immunohistochemical changes
authors: Wu YA, Newman SJ, Lidbury JA, Steiner JM
citation: Wu YA, Newman SJ, Lidbury JA, Steiner JM Serial examination of the pancreas from shelter cats euthanized for population control for the prevalence of histologic and immunohistochemical changes. Veterinary Pathology. 2026. doi:10.1177/03009858261451483
abstract: The clinical relevance of pancreatic histologic changes in cats is unclear. Determination of clinical relevance is complicated by the focal to multifocal nature of these lesions, variable clinical presentation of affected cats, and common comorbidities. Examining the histologic changes on serial pancreatic sections from a cohort of young adult shelter cats without externally observable clinical disease could inform what should be considered normal in cats. Pancreata were obtained from 48 cats euthanized for population control. While hypoalbuminemia was common, liver enzyme activity and gastrointestinal panel results were largely unremarkable. The pancreas was sectioned every 1 cm, routinely processed, and evaluated by a board-certified veterinary pathologist. Pancreatic histologic changes were uncommon in this cohort of cats. Hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections that showed lymphocytic infiltrates were recut for CD3 and CD20 immunohistochemistry. The distribution of CD3 and CD20 positive cells and their percentages were recorded. Of 48 cats, 13 cats (27%) had localized lymphocytic infiltrates with a median percentage of affected sections of 14% (range: 7%–92%). There were no differences in observed percentages or distribution of T- or B-cells. Scattered CD3+ T-cells were incidentally identified in intralobular parenchyma. As mild lymphocytic infiltration was uncommon in this group of cats, it may not indicate a physiological response, as the anticipated response to antigenic stimulation would be expected to occur more diffusely and more commonly. Thus, the role of these infiltrates may reflect bystander inflammation or a primary pathological process (pancreatitis) and likely varies depending on the specific disease context.

mcqs.q: Serial pancreas sections from 48 shelter cats euthanised for population control were examined. What was found?
o: Pancreatic histologic changes were uncommon, and 27% had localised lymphocytic infiltrates, helping define what is normal in young adult cats
Most cats had severe pancreatitis
No cat had any histologic change
mcqs.e: Hypoalbuminaemia was common, but liver enzymes were largely unremarkable.

title: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in Cats, South Korea, 2023
authors: Kang YM, Heo GB, An SH, Lee H, Park E, Cha RM, Jang YY, Sagong M, Kim AY, Kim J, Lee EK, Kim SH, Lee K, Ku B, Lee YJ, Lee K, Lee KN
citation: Kang YM, Heo GB, An SH, Lee H, Park E, Cha RM, Jang YY, Sagong M, Kim AY, Kim J, Lee EK, Kim SH, Lee K, Ku B, Lee YJ, Lee K, Lee KN Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in Cats, South Korea, 2023. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2024. doi:10.3201/eid3012.240154
abstract: In July 2023, cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) were reported at 2 shelters for stray cats in Seoul, South Korea. The cause of infection was suspected to be improperly sterilized raw food made from domestic duck meat, which was manufactured in South Korea. All viruses isolated from cats at the shelters and from the raw food belonged to HPAI A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b. The gene constellation of all viruses was most similar to that of viruses isolated in Korea in November 2022. Of note, the viruses isolated from infected cats harbored mutations E627K or D701N in polymerase basic 2, which are indicative of adaptation to mammals. Postmortem examination revealed systemic pathologic lesions and the presence of widespread virus in different tissues. Thus, consumption of raw duck meat contaminated with HPAI virus likely caused systemic symptoms and death in cats, indicating the introduction of mammal-adapted mutations of the virus.
