mcqs.q: In 2023, highly pathogenic H5N1 was found in cats at two Seoul shelters. What was the suspected source?
o: Improperly sterilised raw food made from domestic duck meat, with mammalian adaptation mutations in the virus
Contact with wild rats, with no mutations
Contaminated litter from imported cats
mcqs.e: The virus was clade 2.3.4.4b, and cats had systemic lesions.

title: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Domestic Dairy Cattle and Cats, United States, 2024
authors: Burrough ER, Magstadt DR, Petersen B, Timmermans SJ, Gauger PC, Zhang J, Siepker C, Mainenti M, Li G, Thompson AC, Gorden PJ, Plummer PJ, Main R
citation: Burrough ER, Magstadt DR, Petersen B, Timmermans SJ, Gauger PC, Zhang J, Siepker C, Mainenti M, Li G, Thompson AC, Gorden PJ, Plummer PJ, Main R Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Domestic Dairy Cattle and Cats, United States, 2024. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2024. doi:10.3201/eid3007.240508
abstract: We report highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus in dairy cattle and cats in Kansas and Texas, United States, which reflects the continued spread of clade 2.3.4.4b viruses that entered the country in late 2021. Infected cattle experienced nonspecific illness, reduced feed intake and rumination, and an abrupt drop in milk production, but fatal systemic influenza infection developed in domestic cats fed raw (unpasteurized) colostrum and milk from affected cows. Cow-to-cow transmission appears to have occurred because infections were observed in cattle on Michigan, Idaho, and Ohio farms where avian influenza virus-infected cows were transported. Although the US Food and Drug Administration has indicated the commercial milk supply remains safe, the detection of influenza virus in unpasteurized bovine milk is a concern because of potential cross-species transmission. Continued surveillance of highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses in domestic production animals is needed to prevent cross-species and mammal-to-mammal transmission.

mcqs.q: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b was reported in dairy cattle and cats in Kansas and Texas in 2024. How did cats become infected?
o: By being fed raw (unpasteurised) colostrum and milk from affected cows, developing fatal systemic infection
By inhaling aerosols from wild birds only
By eating properly pasteurised milk
mcqs.e: Cattle showed reduced feed intake, rumination and milk production, and cow-to-cow transmission appears to have occurred.

title: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus in Domestic Cat, France, 2022
authors: Briand FX, Souchaud F, Pierre I, Beven V, Hirchaud E, Hérault F, Planel R, Rigaudeau A, Bernard-Stoecklin S, Van der Werf S, Lina B, Gerbier G, Eterradossi N, Schmitz A, Niqueux E, Grasland B
citation: Briand FX, Souchaud F, Pierre I, Beven V, Hirchaud E, Hérault F, Planel R, Rigaudeau A, Bernard-Stoecklin S, Van der Werf S, Lina B, Gerbier G, Eterradossi N, Schmitz A, Niqueux E, Grasland B Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus in Domestic Cat, France, 2022. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2023. doi:10.3201/eid2908.230188
abstract: We detected highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus in a domestic cat that lived near a duck farm infected by a closely related virus in France during December 2022. Enhanced surveillance of symptomatic domestic carnivores in contact with infected birds is recommended to prevent further spread to mammals and humans.

mcqs.q: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b was found in a domestic cat in France living near an infected duck farm. What does the report recommend?
o: Enhanced surveillance of symptomatic domestic carnivores in contact with infected birds, to prevent spread to mammals and humans
No surveillance, since a single cat is unimportant
Culling of all cats near duck farms
mcqs.e: The virus was closely related to that on the farm in December 2022.

title: Risk Factors for SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Illness in Cats and Dogs
authors: Bienzle D, Rousseau J, Marom D, MacNicol J, Jacobson L, Sparling S, Prystajecky N, Fraser E, Weese JS
citation: Bienzle D, Rousseau J, Marom D, MacNicol J, Jacobson L, Sparling S, Prystajecky N, Fraser E, Weese JS Risk Factors for SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Illness in Cats and Dogs. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2022. doi:10.3201/eid2806.220423
abstract: We tested swab specimens from pets in households in Ontario, Canada, with human COVID-19 cases by quantitative PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and surveyed pet owners for risk factors associated with infection and seropositivity. We tested serum samples for spike protein IgG and IgM in household pets and also in animals from shelters and low-cost neuter clinics. Among household pets, 2% (1/49) of swab specimens from dogs and 7.7% (5/65) from cats were PCR positive, but 41% of dog serum samples and 52% of cat serum samples were positive for SARS-CoV-2 IgG or IgM. The likelihood of SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity in pet samples was higher for cats but not dogs that slept on owners' beds and for dogs and cats that contracted a new illness. Seropositivity in neuter-clinic samples was 16% (35/221); in shelter samples, 9.3% (7/75). Our findings indicate a high likelihood for pets in households of humans with COVID-19 to seroconvert and become ill.

mcqs.q: Pets in Ontario households with human COVID-19 cases were tested for SARS-CoV-2. Which finding is correct?
o: Most swabs were PCR positive, and serology was negative
Dogs had higher seropositivity than cats, unrelated to sleeping arrangements
Few swabs were PCR positive (2% dogs, 7.7% cats), but about half of serum samples were seropositive, and seropositivity was higher in cats that slept on owners' beds
mcqs.e: Seropositivity in neuter-clinic samples was 16% and in shelter samples 9.3%.

title: Genetically Similar High-Risk Strains of Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacterales in Humans and Companion Animals, United States
authors: Xiaoli L, James AE, Stahl AL, Okumura M, Cole SD, Dietrich JM, Leeper MM, Putney JK, Walters MS, Stanton RA
citation: Xiaoli L, James AE, Stahl AL, Okumura M, Cole SD, Dietrich JM, Leeper MM, Putney JK, Walters MS, Stanton RA Genetically Similar High-Risk Strains of Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacterales in Humans and Companion Animals, United States. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2026. doi:10.3201/eid3203.251458
abstract: To elucidate the zoonotic potential of carbapenemase-producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CP-CRE) in US companion animals (i.e., dogs and cats), we queried the National Center for Biotechnology Pathogen Detection database to identify One Health clusters containing CP-CRE isolates from companion animals and humans. The 11 One Health clusters we found included most (69% [169/246]) publicly available CP-CRE sequences from US companion animals and were from 8 internationally disseminated, high-risk sequence types from 3 bacterial species (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterobacter cloacae). All clustered isolates had New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-family carbapenemases, and most (92%) carried the blaNDM-5 allele. The One Health clusters included several closely related subclusters with geographically linked isolates from both humans and companion animals. Those results suggest that CP-CRE is an emerging One Health issue and that direct or indirect transmission of CP-CRE is occurring between humans and companion animals in the United States.

mcqs.q: A database analysis found One Health clusters of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales in US dogs, cats and humans, and most carried blaNDM-5. What does this suggest?
o: Carbapenemase-producing bacteria are restricted to hospitalised humans, and pets are unaffected
Isolates from pets are genetically unrelated to human isolates
Direct or indirect transmission is occurring between humans and companion animals, making it an emerging One Health issue
mcqs.e: Eleven clusters held 69% of US companion animal sequences, and included geographically linked human and animal isolates.

title: Giardia duodenalis in colony stray cats from Italy
authors: Guadano Procesi I, Carnio A, Berrilli F, Montalbano Di Filippo M, Scarito A, Amoruso C, Barni M, Ruffini M, Barlozzari G, Scarpulla M, De Liberato C
citation: Guadano Procesi I, Carnio A, Berrilli F, Montalbano Di Filippo M, Scarito A, Amoruso C, Barni M, Ruffini M, Barlozzari G, Scarpulla M, De Liberato C Giardia duodenalis in colony stray cats from Italy. Zoonoses and Public Health. 2022. doi:10.1111/zph.12894
abstract: Study detected and genetically characterized G. duodenalis from stray cat colonies in central Italy (2018–2019). Of 133 fecal samples, 47 samples (35.3%) were positive for G. duodenalis cysts. Molecular analysis revealed 37 were positive for zoonotic Assemblage A and 2 showed a mixed infection (A + B). Sequence analysis identified Sub-assemblage AII and AIII variants. The authors noted all positive cats resulted to be infected with zoonotic assemblages, indicating stray cats as a potential human giardiasis source.

mcqs.q: Of 133 faecal samples from stray cat colonies in central Italy, 47 were positive for Giardia duodenalis, and most positives had Assemblage A. What does this imply?
o: Stray cats can be a potential source of zoonotic giardiasis, because the assemblages found infect humans
Stray cat Giardia is host-specific and poses no zoonotic risk
Giardia in cats was all Assemblage F, which is cat-specific
mcqs.e: Thirty-seven cats had zoonotic Assemblage A, and two had a mixed A and B infection.

title: Serological and Molecular Surveillance of Influenza A Virus in Dogs and Cats in Central Chile
authors: Baumberger C, Di Pillo F, Sanchez F, Sepúlveda A, Marambio V, Orozco K, Tapia D, Hamilton-West C, Sharp B, Schultz-Cherry S, Jiménez-Bluhm P
citation: Baumberger C, Di Pillo F, Sanchez F, Sepúlveda A, Marambio V, Orozco K, Tapia D, Hamilton-West C, Sharp B, Schultz-Cherry S, Jiménez-Bluhm P Serological and Molecular Surveillance of Influenza A Virus in Dogs and Cats in Central Chile. Zoonoses and Public Health. 2026. doi:10.1111/zph.70073
abstract: Study evaluated influenza A virus circulation in companion animals from Chilean shelters and households (June–November 2020). IAV was detected by RT-qPCR in 3.2% (11/342) of dogs and 5.8% (4/69) of cats. Serological analysis revealed 55.5% (96/173) of dogs and 50.0% (10/20) of cats with IAV seropositivity. The study presented the first report of IAV detection in cats in South America and emphasized incorporating pets into surveillance frameworks under One Health approaches.

mcqs.q: Influenza A virus was sought in dogs and cats from Chilean shelters and households in 2020. What was notable?
o: It was the first report of influenza A detection in cats in South America, with RT-qPCR detection in 5.8% of cats and high seropositivity in dogs and cats
No animal had evidence of influenza infection
Only dogs were infected, and cats were negative
mcqs.e: The authors emphasise including pets in One Health surveillance frameworks.

title: Serological exposure to influenza A in cats from an area with wild birds positive for avian influenza
authors: Villanueva-Saz S, Martínez M, Rueda P, Pérez MD, Lacasta D, Marteles D, Ruíz H, Gonzalez A, Verde MT, Pardo J, Arias M, Peña-Fresneda N, Fernández A, Trotta M
citation: Villanueva-Saz S, Martínez M, Rueda P, Pérez MD, Lacasta D, Marteles D, Ruíz H, Gonzalez A, Verde MT, Pardo J, Arias M, Peña-Fresneda N, Fernández A, Trotta M Serological exposure to influenza A in cats from an area with wild birds positive for avian influenza. Zoonoses and Public Health. 2024. doi:10.1111/zph.13085
abstract: A cross-sectional study of 183 stray cats in Spain from 2022–2023 measured anti-influenza A antibodies using ELISA. Four of the 183 animals tested showed anti-influenza A antibodies by ELISA, yielding a seroprevalence of influenza A of 2.19%. The researchers concluded that based on this low prevalence, cats did not have an important epidemiological role in influenza A transmission during this period.

mcqs.q: Sera from 183 stray cats in Spain, in an area with avian influenza in wild birds, were tested for influenza A antibodies. What was concluded?
o: Seroprevalence was low (2.19%), so cats had no important epidemiological role in influenza A transmission at the time
Seroprevalence was above 50%, so cats are a major reservoir
No cat had antibodies, so cats cannot be infected
mcqs.e: Four of 183 cats were positive by ELISA.

title: Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and a possible variant in shelter cats
authors: Okwumabua O, Bradley-Siemens N, Cruz C, Chittick L, Thompson M
citation: Okwumabua O, Bradley-Siemens N, Cruz C, Chittick L, Thompson M Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and a possible variant in shelter cats. PLoS ONE. 2025. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0317104
abstract: Researchers tested conjunctival, pharyngeal, and serum samples from 350 cats housed in an animal shelter, collected between July and December 2020, for SARS-CoV-2 using rRT-PCR targeting the N1 and N2 genes plus a surrogate virus neutralization test. Results showed that 203 (58%) swab samples were negative (N1 and N2 not detected), 2 (0.6%) were positive (N1 and N2 detected) and 145 (41%) were inconclusive (only N1 detected). Analysis revealed base-pair deletions and substitutions in the N2 probe binding region of the feline samples RNA extracts in comparison with the positive control. When using a redesigned cat-derived probe, 123 of 127 (96.9%) of the N2 negative samples returned positive results. The study concludes that cats can harbor the virus and serve as a potential source for virus spread, and suggests cats may carry a yet-to-be-described virus that is somewhat related to SARS-CoV-2.

mcqs.q: Shelter cats (n = 350) tested inconclusive (N1 gene detected only) for SARS-CoV-2 in 41%. What did a redesigned cat-derived probe show?
o: Most N2-negative samples became positive, suggesting sequence variation in the N2 probe region and possibly a related virus
All samples remained negative, so the inconclusive results were errors
The results proved human variants of concern in all cats
mcqs.e: Base-pair deletions and substitutions were found in the N2 probe binding region.

title: A prospective study of mental wellbeing, quality of life, human-animal attachment, and grief among foster caregivers at animal shelters
authors: Powell L, Ackerman R, Reinhard CL, Serpell J, Watson B
citation: Powell L, Ackerman R, Reinhard CL, Serpell J, Watson B A prospective study of mental wellbeing, quality of life, human-animal attachment, and grief among foster caregivers at animal shelters. PLoS ONE. 2024. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0301661
abstract: This longitudinal study examined 131 foster caregivers from five U.S. animal shelters between March 2022 and 2023. Participants completed three online surveys at baseline, during fostering, and post-placement. Key findings: positive affect decreased significantly after foster animals departed (p<0.01), particularly among dog caregivers. Negative affect remained stable throughout. Dog caregivers reported greater emotional and social/physical quality-of-life benefits than cat caregivers. Foster caregivers demonstrated secure attachment patterns with low anxious and avoidant attachment scores. Most caregivers (86%) indicated likelihood of future fostering participation. Caregivers reported experiencing both anticipatory and ambiguous grief upon animal departure. The researchers concluded that while fostering at animal shelters may serve as a One Health intervention by offering companionship, affection, and emotional support, mental wellbeing improvements were not evident, warranting caution about positioning foster care as a mental health promotion strategy.

mcqs.q: A prospective study followed 131 foster caregivers from five US shelters through baseline, fostering and post-placement. What was concluded about mental wellbeing?
o: Positive affect fell after animals left, and no improvement in mental wellbeing was evident, so fostering should be positioned with caution as a mental health strategy
Wellbeing improved markedly during fostering, so fostering is a proven mental health intervention
Cat caregivers had more benefits than dog caregivers, and grief was absent
mcqs.e: Caregivers reported anticipatory and ambiguous grief, and 86% were likely to foster again.

title: Quantification of a shelter cat population: Trends in intake, length of stay and outcome data of cats in seven Dutch shelters between 2006 and 2021
authors: van der Leij WJR, Vernooij JCM, Vinke CM, Corbee RJ, Hesselink JW
citation: van der Leij WJR, Vernooij JCM, Vinke CM, Corbee RJ, Hesselink JW Quantification of a shelter cat population: Trends in intake, length of stay and outcome data of cats in seven Dutch shelters between 2006 and 2021. PLoS ONE. 2023. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0285938
abstract: Shelters utilize metrics for self-assessment to enhance animal population health and identify disease outbreak risk factors. However, broader metric applications are needed for benchmarking and developing best practices. This retrospective study analyzed data from seven Dutch shelters over 2006–2021, examining intake sources, outcomes, and length of stay for over 74,000 cats. Key findings demonstrate that feline intake decreased by 39% per 1,000 residents, while euthanasia cases declined approximately 50%. Length of stay showed reducing trends, and return-to-owner rates increased alongside the risk-based live release rate. The researchers conclude these metrics effectively monitor shelter management, animal health and welfare, and can measure progress both nationally and across Europe.

mcqs.q: Data from seven Dutch shelters over 2006 to 2021 (over 74,000 cats) were analysed. Which trends were found?
o: Intake per 1,000 residents fell 39%, euthanasia fell about 50%, length of stay decreased, and return-to-owner rates rose
Intake rose, euthanasia rose and length of stay increased
Intake fell, but euthanasia and length of stay were unchanged
mcqs.e: The metrics can be used to monitor shelter management, health and welfare, and to benchmark nationally and across Europe.

title: Social mechanisms for integrating community cats into community governance in urban China
citation: Wu D, Gu J Social mechanisms for integrating community cats into community governance in urban China. PLoS ONE. 2024. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0308120
abstract: The presence of unowned cats roaming urban spaces has generated considerable debate. This research examines how community cats become incorporated into neighborhood governance through resident interactions. Using participatory observation and interviews, the study applies a social capital framework examining norms, trust, and networks. The findings reveal that social norms and trust activate community social capital, creating a social network centered on community cat care. Notably, this network extends care beyond cats to encompass other community members. The researchers term this mechanism 'care extension.' The study concludes that this approach fosters neighborly bonds transcending ecological relationships, ultimately contributing to a compassionate and harmonious multi-species urban community.

mcqs.q: A study in urban China examined how community cats become part of neighbourhood governance. What mechanism did it identify?
o: 'Care extension', where norms and trust create a social network around cat care that extends care to other community members
Government enforcement only
Competition between residents
mcqs.e: The study applied a social capital framework of norms, trust and networks.

title: Rethinking the Animal Shelter's Role in Free-Roaming Cat Management
citation: Hurley KF, Levy JK Rethinking the Animal Shelter's Role in Free-Roaming Cat Management. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2022. doi:10.3389/fvets.2022.847081
abstract: This article examines three shelter-based strategies for managing free-roaming cats: removal through impoundment, sterilization with return to location of origin, and leaving cats in place with community referrals. The authors argue that traditional removal programs are ineffective at population control, noting that removal short of eradication may not only fail to decrease the population, it can magnify concerns. They present evidence that sterilization-and-return programs show promise for reducing shelter intake while improving cat welfare. The paper advocates for an evidence-based approach recognizing that most free-roaming cats remain in communities regardless of shelter intervention, and recommends individualized case management tailored to specific circumstances rather than standardized policies.

mcqs.q: An article rethinks the shelter's role in free-roaming cat management. What is its argument?
o: Removal by impoundment is the most effective strategy
Removal short of eradication may not reduce populations, sterilisation-and-return shows promise for reducing intake, and case management should be individualised
Standardised policies are best
mcqs.e: Most free-roaming cats remain in communities regardless of shelter intervention.

title: COVID-19 associated reduction in elective spay-neuter surgeries for dogs and cats
authors: Guerios SD, Porcher TR, Clemmer G, Denagamage T, Levy JK
citation: Guerios SD, Porcher TR, Clemmer G, Denagamage T, Levy JK COVID-19 associated reduction in elective spay-neuter surgeries for dogs and cats. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2022. doi:10.3389/fvets.2022.912893
abstract: The study examined pandemic impacts on sterilization procedures using data from 212 clinics. Surgeries decreased 13% to 1,059,388 in 2020 compared to the 2019 baseline of approximately 1.2 million procedures. April 2020 experienced the steepest decline at negative 80%. By 2021, procedures partially recovered but remained 3% below the baseline year. The analysis projected that if similar patterns affected all U.S. spay-neuter providers, there could be a deficit of more than 2.7 million unperformed surgeries. The study emphasizes concerns about potential increases in unwanted litters and reversals in population control achievements, noting that as of August 2022, spay-neuter clinics had not yet returned to baseline productivity due to ongoing workforce shortages of veterinarians and staff.

mcqs.q: Data from 212 clinics showed how COVID-19 affected elective spay-neuter surgery. Which finding is correct?
o: Surgeries rose 13% in 2020, and recovered fully by 2021
Surgeries fell 13% in 2020 (April 2020 down 80%), and by 2021 remained 3% below 2019, with workforce shortages continuing
Surgeries were unchanged, and the workforce increased
mcqs.e: The analysis projected a deficit of more than 2.7 million surgeries nationally.

title: The Impact of Incorporating Multiple Best Practices on Live Outcomes for a Municipal Animal Shelter in Memphis, TN
authors: Kreisler RE, Pugh AA, Pemberton K, Pizano S
citation: Kreisler RE, Pugh AA, Pemberton K, Pizano S The Impact of Incorporating Multiple Best Practices on Live Outcomes for a Municipal Animal Shelter in Memphis, TN. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2022. doi:10.3389/fvets.2022.786866
abstract: Modern shelters are encouraged to adopt best practices promoting animal life-saving. Memphis Animal Services implemented five strategies in 2017 and tracked their effects: managed strategic intake, pet owner safety nets, community cat return-to-field programs, transforming field services from enforcement to assistance, and streamlined adoption/transfer processes. For cats, the median live release rate increased from 35% to 92% post-intervention. The correlation between intake and euthanasia shifted from significant and very strong (r = 0.982) to non-significant (−0.165). For dogs, rates improved from 25% to 87%. Kitten euthanasia decreased dramatically from a median of 59% to 3% of kittens entering the shelter. Dog return-to-owner rates improved from 10% to 13%. The study demonstrates that implementation of these best practices accelerated progress toward a live release rate of at least 90%, particularly for cats, dramatically decreased kitten euthanasia, increased the return-to-owner rate for dogs, and severed the historical correlation between euthanasia and intake.

mcqs.q: Memphis Animal Services implemented five best practices in 2017. What were the results?
o: Live release rates did not change
Cat live release rose from 35% to 92%, dog live release from 25% to 87%, kitten euthanasia fell from 59% to 3%, and the correlation between intake and euthanasia disappeared
Euthanasia correlated more strongly with intake
mcqs.e: Strategies included managed intake, owner safety nets, return-to-field and streamlined adoption.

title: Animal shelter management of feline leukemia virus and feline immunodeficiency virus infections in cats
authors: Dezubiria P, Amirian ES, Spera K, Crawford PC, Levy JK
citation: Dezubiria P, Amirian ES, Spera K, Crawford PC, Levy JK Animal shelter management of feline leukemia virus and feline immunodeficiency virus infections in cats. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2023. doi:10.3389/fvets.2022.1003388
abstract: This study examined feline retroviral management practices among 139 Florida animal shelters. The survey covered testing protocols, diagnostic techniques, and outcome options for cats with positive results. Key findings showed that 83% of shelters performed at least some testing, primarily using combination point-of-care devices for simultaneous FeLV antigen and FIV antibody screening. Testing selection varied by population: screening adoptable cats (108 shelters; 94%) was most common, while testing cats in trap-neuter-return programs was least common (18%). For positive cats, common outcomes included adoption (64%), transfer (54%), and euthanasia (43%). Euthanasia was more prevalent for FeLV-positive cats than FIV-positive ones, and more common in municipal shelters with lower live outcome rates. The authors concluded that while most shelters offered live outcome options, increased access to training and practical tools could enhance testing protocols and support better outcomes for this vulnerable population.

mcqs.q: A survey of 139 Florida shelters examined FeLV and FIV management. Which finding is correct?
o: Few shelters tested, and all positive cats were euthanised
83% tested at least some cats, screening adoptable cats was most common, and euthanasia was more common for FeLV-positive than FIV-positive cats and in municipal shelters
Testing of trap-neuter-return cats was the most common
mcqs.e: Common outcomes for positive cats were adoption (64%), transfer (54%) and euthanasia (43%).

title: Cross-sectional survey exploring current intake practices for dogs admitted to animal shelters in Texas: a descriptive study
authors: Cranford M, Bing A, Cisneros A, Carroll AD, Porter H, Stellato AC
citation: Cranford M, Bing A, Cisneros A, Carroll AD, Porter H, Stellato AC Cross-sectional survey exploring current intake practices for dogs admitted to animal shelters in Texas: a descriptive study. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2023. doi:10.3389/fvets.2023.1296425
abstract: The researchers examined shelter intake procedures in Texas through a survey of 64 shelter employees across 47 counties. Staff reported varying handling approaches based on dog demeanor—using treats and gentle techniques for calm animals, but escalating to muzzles and catch poles for aggressive dogs. Most participants asked about behavioral history during owner surrenders, particularly regarding aggression. After exams, approximately 45% housed dogs on adoption floors. The authors note that while many current practices align with stress-reduction recommendations, future research should provide evidence-based protocols to support dog welfare during intake procedures and handler safety.

mcqs.q: A survey of 64 Texas shelter employees described dog intake procedures. Which finding is correct?
o: All dogs were handled identically
No shelter asked about behaviour history
Handling varied with demeanour, from treats and gentle techniques to muzzles and catch poles for aggressive dogs, and most asked about behaviour history during surrenders
mcqs.e: About 45% housed dogs on adoption floors after examination.

title: Effects of single- or pair-housing on the welfare of shelter dogs: Behavioral and physiological indicators
authors: Hecker G, Martineau K, Scheskie M, Hammerslough R, Feuerbacher EN
citation: Hecker G, Martineau K, Scheskie M, Hammerslough R, Feuerbacher EN Effects of single- or pair-housing on the welfare of shelter dogs: Behavioral and physiological indicators. PLoS ONE. 2024. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0301137
abstract: The researchers investigated whether housing shelter dogs in compatible pairs versus alone affects their wellbeing. They observed 61 dogs (30 single-housed; 31 pair-housed) over seven days, collecting daily behavioral videos and urine samples for cortisol:creatinine analysis. Results showed pair-housed dogs exhibited significantly fewer stress indicators including lip licking, whining, and ears back compared to solitary dogs. The pair-housed group demonstrated greater reductions in cortisol levels and had shorter adoption timeframes by approximately four days. The study found that well-matched pair-housing can have both proximate and ultimate welfare benefits for shelter dogs, with minimal aggression concerns and evidence of affiliative behaviors between compatible pairs.

mcqs.q: Sixty-one shelter dogs were housed singly or in compatible pairs for seven days. What was found?
o: Pair-housed dogs had fewer stress behaviours, greater cortisol reductions and about four days shorter time to adoption, with minimal aggression
Single housing gave lower stress
Pairs had more aggression
mcqs.e: Behaviours included lip licking, whining and ears back.

title: Shelter dog behavior after adoption: Using the C-BARQ to track dog behavior changes through the first six months after adoption
authors: Bohland KR, Lilly ML, Herron ME, Arruda AG, O'Quin JM
citation: Bohland KR, Lilly ML, Herron ME, Arruda AG, O'Quin JM Shelter dog behavior after adoption: Using the C-BARQ to track dog behavior changes through the first six months after adoption. PLoS ONE. 2023. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0289356
abstract: This prospective observational cohort study examined behavioral changes in shelter-adopted dogs during their initial six months in new homes. Ninety-nine dog owners from five Ohio shelters completed surveys using the Canine Behavioral Assessment and Research Questionnaire (C-BARQ) at 7, 30, 90, and 180 days post-adoption. Key findings revealed high prevalence rates for various behaviors, including stranger-directed aggression (81.7%), owner-directed aggression (32.3%), dog-directed aggression (75%) and separation-related behaviors. Over the study period, stranger-directed aggression, excitability, touch sensitivity, training difficulty, and chasing increased, while separation-related behaviors and attachment decreased. Psychotropic medication use in shelters predicted increased stranger-directed aggression post-adoption. Despite these behavioral changes, owners reported high satisfaction levels with their dogs' overall behavior and adjustment.

mcqs.q: Ninety-nine adopters used the C-BARQ at 7, 30, 90 and 180 days after adoption. Which finding is correct?
o: All problem behaviours decreased and satisfaction was low
Nothing changed
Stranger-directed aggression, excitability and training difficulty increased while separation-related behaviours and attachment decreased, and adopters remained highly satisfied
mcqs.e: Psychotropic medication use in shelters predicted more stranger-directed aggression.

title: The Influence of Brief Outing and Temporary Fostering Programs on Shelter Dog Welfare
authors: Gunter LM, Blade EM, Gilchrist RJ, Nixon BJ, Reed JL, Platzer JM, Wurpts IC, Feuerbacher EN, Wynne CDL
citation: Gunter LM, Blade EM, Gilchrist RJ, Nixon BJ, Reed JL, Platzer JM, Wurpts IC, Feuerbacher EN, Wynne CDL The Influence of Brief Outing and Temporary Fostering Programs on Shelter Dog Welfare. Animals. 2023. doi:10.3390/ani13223528
abstract: The research team examined whether brief outings and temporary foster stays improved shelter dog outcomes. Analyzing data from 1,955 dogs receiving interventions and 25,946 control dogs across 51 shelters, they found that brief outings and temporary fostering stays increased dogs' likelihood of adoption by approximately five and fourteen times respectively. While intervention dogs had longer pre-intervention shelter stays, post-intervention stays averaged just 10 days before adoption. Programs performed better with greater community involvement and adequate resources. The authors conclude these interventions represent evidence-based best practices that can positively impact the outcomes of shelter dogs.

mcqs.q: Data on 1,955 dogs given brief outings or temporary foster stays and 25,946 controls were analysed. What was found?
o: Outings and fostering reduced adoption
Adoption likelihood increased about five times with outings and fourteen times with fostering, and programmes performed better with community involvement and resources
There was no effect
mcqs.e: Intervention dogs averaged 10 days to adoption after the intervention.

title: Cat Foster Program Outcomes: Behavior, Stress, and Cat–Human Interaction
authors: Vitale KR, Frank DH, Conroy J, Udell MAR
citation: Vitale KR, Frank DH, Conroy J, Udell MAR Cat Foster Program Outcomes: Behavior, Stress, and Cat–Human Interaction. Animals. 2022. doi:10.3390/ani12172166
abstract: The researchers investigated whether placing shelter cats in foster homes—even temporarily—produces stress or behavioral problems. They compared cats placed in overnight or week-long foster care with cats remaining in shelters, measuring stress through cortisol levels and behavioral assessments. Key findings indicate that foster cats did not display decreased social behavior, increased fear or aggression, or increased cortisol levels while in the foster home. Cats experienced litter box aversion on the first night but resumed normal behavior afterward. Foster volunteers engaged in petting, playing, and cuddling activities with their temporary charges. The research demonstrates that short-term fostering appears safe and potentially beneficial, suggesting shelters can use foster programs during overcrowding without harming cat welfare. The authors conclude this information could contribute to life-saving efforts by enabling cats to temporarily leave shelters when space is limited.

mcqs.q: A study compared cats in overnight or week-long foster homes with cats staying in the shelter. Which finding is correct?
o: Foster cats had higher cortisol and more aggression than shelter cats
Foster cats showed no decrease in social behaviour and no increase in fear, aggression or cortisol, apart from litter box aversion on the first night
Foster cats had persistent litter box aversion and reduced social behaviour
mcqs.e: Short-term fostering appears safe, so shelters can use it during overcrowding.

title: Animal Cruelty in New York City: Cruelty Cases Presented to the ASPCA in Partnership with the NYPD 2013–2022
authors: Caldwell S, Patterson-Kane E, Brandler E, Gupta M, Lockwood R
citation: Caldwell S, Patterson-Kane E, Brandler E, Gupta M, Lockwood R Animal Cruelty in New York City: Cruelty Cases Presented to the ASPCA in Partnership with the NYPD 2013–2022. Animals. 2025. doi:10.3390/ani15050662
abstract: The research examined companion animal abuse reports in New York City over a nine-year period (2013–2022). The ASPCA received 2,783 cases involving 5,745 animals through collaboration with the NYPD. The majority involved dogs (82%), followed by cats (15%) and other species (4%). Dogs were most frequently reported for suspected neglect, representing 63% of canine cases. Cats showed a different pattern, with 58% of feline cases involving suspected non-accidental injury. Referral sources included law enforcement (37%), municipal shelters (14%), and veterinarians (11%). The authors concluded that neglect represents a commonly documented form of animal abuse, while cat abuse appears less well understood and may be under-reported or more severe.

mcqs.q: A review of 2,783 cruelty cases the ASPCA received in partnership with the NYPD from 2013 to 2022 compared species. Which pattern was found?
o: Dogs were most often reported for suspected non-accidental injury, and cats most often for suspected neglect
Dogs and cats were reported for neglect and non-accidental injury in about equal proportions
Dogs were most often reported for suspected neglect, and cats most often for suspected non-accidental injury
mcqs.e: Neglect made up 63% of canine cases, and 58% of feline cases involved suspected non-accidental injury. The authors suggest cat abuse may be under-reported or more severe.

title: Animal Abuse Investigations: Challenges and Recommendations to Improve Animal and Human Welfare
citation: Niemiec R, Kogan LR Animal Abuse Investigations: Challenges and Recommendations to Improve Animal and Human Welfare. Animals. 2024. doi:10.3390/ani14243602
abstract: The research explores systemic barriers affecting animal cruelty case management in Colorado through interviews with 24 law enforcement and Bureau of Animal Protection personnel. Researchers identified four primary obstacles: a lack of places to take removed animals and resources to care for them; difficulties collaborating with district attorneys; insufficient training on case procedures; and inadequate investigative staff. The study recommends expanding temporary housing capacity, enhancing professional training, employing specialized investigators and mental health professionals, and potentially amending state statutes. Significantly, the authors advocate implementing a trauma-informed model to address psychological impacts on workers handling these distressing cases, recognizing the interconnected welfare of animals, professionals, and communities.

mcqs.q: Interviews with 24 Colorado law enforcement and animal protection personnel identified obstacles to abuse investigations. Which combination is correct, along with a recommendation for worker wellbeing?
o: Too many veterinarians involved, delays in laboratory results and unclear species definitions; mandatory rotation of officers
Public reluctance to report, absence of state statutes and lack of shelters; higher penalties
Too few places and resources for removed animals, difficulty working with district attorneys, limited training and too few investigators; a trauma-informed model
mcqs.e: The four obstacles were housing and resources for animals, working with district attorneys, training, and investigative staffing. The authors advocate a trauma-informed model for workers.

title: Forensic Death Investigations of Dog Bite Injuries in 31 Cats
authors: Hsiou CL, Hsu CC, Liao PW, Yang FH, Lee AN, Huang WH
citation: Hsiou CL, Hsu CC, Liao PW, Yang FH, Lee AN, Huang WH Forensic Death Investigations of Dog Bite Injuries in 31 Cats. Animals. 2022. doi:10.3390/ani12182404
abstract: This forensic veterinary study analyzed bite injury patterns in 31 necropsied cats and applied DNA analysis for species identification. Researchers found that puncture wounds, linear or small round contusions/abrasions, and lacerations/avulsions are characteristic bite-related injuries. The examination of 31 cats revealed the most commonly injured regions included the ventral thorax, hindlimbs, shoulder-to-dorsal thorax, back, abdomen, neck, and hip/tail/perineum. Canine mitochondrial DNA was successfully identified in wound swabs and hair samples from broken claws. The study provided an applicable method for canine DNA identification in cats and reference data for future veterinary forensic investigations of dog bite injuries.

mcqs.q: A forensic necropsy of a cat shows puncture wounds, small round contusions and lacerations, and a dog attack is suspected. Which method did a study of 31 cats use to confirm the species responsible?
o: Canine mitochondrial DNA identified from wound swabs and hair caught in broken claws
Measurement of the puncture spacing alone, because it identifies the dog breed
Radiographs of the skull, which show the biting species
mcqs.e: The injured regions included the ventral thorax, hindlimbs, shoulder to dorsal thorax, back, abdomen, neck and hip, tail and perineum.

title: Documenting non-accidental injury patterns in a dog abuse investigation: A collaborative approach between forensic anthropology and veterinary pathology
authors: Bartelink EJ, Clinkinbeard S, Spessard C, Kilmartin A, Spangler WL
citation: Bartelink EJ, Clinkinbeard S, Spessard C, Kilmartin A, Spangler WL Documenting non-accidental injury patterns in a dog abuse investigation: A collaborative approach between forensic anthropology and veterinary pathology. Journal of Forensic Sciences. 2022. doi:10.1111/1556-4029.14948
abstract: This investigation involved four deceased canines whose remains were excavated from a residential property suspected of animal abuse. Researchers used forensic anthropology and veterinary pathology collaboration to examine skeletonized remains. The analysis revealed evidence of perimortem blunt force trauma on all four skeletons, with injuries concentrated on the axial skeleton and pelvis. One dog exhibited healed rib fractures suggesting previous trauma weeks before death—findings inconsistent with the dog owner's account and instrumental in resolving the case. The study demonstrates how collaboration between forensic anthropologists and veterinary pathologists can effectively document skeletal trauma and non-accidental injury patterns in animal abuse investigations.

mcqs.q: Four canine skeletons are excavated from a property suspected of abuse. All show perimortem blunt force trauma of the axial skeleton and pelvis, and one has healed rib fractures. How should the healed fractures be interpreted?
o: As evidence of earlier trauma, weeks before death, which is inconsistent with the owner's account
As postmortem damage from excavation and burial
As evidence of nutritional bone disease unrelated to the cause of death
mcqs.e: Healed rib fractures indicate an injury that occurred weeks before death, and this finding was instrumental in resolving the case.

title: A multidisciplinary investigation of chronic animal abuse: Collaboration between veterinary forensics and forensic anthropology
citation: Smith-Blackmore M, Bethard JD A multidisciplinary investigation of chronic animal abuse: Collaboration between veterinary forensics and forensic anthropology. Journal of Forensic Sciences. 2021. doi:10.1111/1556-4029.14576
abstract: The study describes a case involving an injured juvenile female mixed breed dog discovered in an urban area. The animal was deemed to have irreparable injuries and was humanely euthanized. A forensic veterinarian collaborated with a forensic anthropologist to document skeletal trauma sustained before death. The examination revealed numerous injuries in various stages of healing diagnostic of non-accidental injuries. The authors conclude that forensic anthropologists can provide valuable support in analyzing bone remains in veterinary forensic cases involving suspected abuse.

mcqs.q: A juvenile dog with irreparable injuries is euthanised, and a forensic veterinarian works with a forensic anthropologist to examine the skeleton. Multiple injuries are found at different stages of healing. What is the most appropriate conclusion?
o: The injuries are consistent with a single road traffic accident
The injuries are diagnostic of non-accidental injury over time, and forensic anthropologists can support the analysis of bone in abuse cases
The injuries cannot be dated, so the skeleton has no forensic value
mcqs.e: Numerous injuries in various stages of healing point to repeated trauma, and the authors conclude that anthropologists can help analyse bone in veterinary forensic cases.

title: Assessing the Impact of a Virtual Shelter Medicine Rotation on Veterinary Students' Knowledge, Skills, and Attitudes Regarding Access to Veterinary Care
authors: Hoffman CL, Spencer TG, Makolinski KV
citation: Hoffman CL, Spencer TG, Makolinski KV Assessing the Impact of a Virtual Shelter Medicine Rotation on Veterinary Students' Knowledge, Skills, and Attitudes Regarding Access to Veterinary Care. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2021. doi:10.3389/fvets.2021.783233
abstract: The study examined how incorporating detailed information about veterinary care accessibility within a shelter medicine rotation affected fourth-year veterinary students. Participants engaged in either a control group virtual rotation or an experimental group that included an interactive online module focused on access barriers. Results indicated that all students developed more positive perspectives on nonprofit veterinary clinics and believed veterinarians should offer affordable treatment options. The experimental group specifically showed increased awareness of the potential for implicit bias toward pet owners and demonstrated reduced judgmental tendencies toward clients. These students also reported greater confidence in providing incremental care options. The authors conclude that curriculum emphasizing access to veterinary care enhances students' preparedness to serve diverse clientele through varied treatment and payment approaches.

mcqs.q: Fourth-year veterinary students took a virtual shelter medicine rotation with or without an interactive access-to-care module. What did the module group show?
o: Less confidence providing care options
More judgmental attitudes
More awareness of implicit bias, less judgmental tendencies toward clients and greater confidence providing incremental care options
mcqs.e: All students developed more positive perspectives on nonprofit clinics.

title: Shelter Medicine Programs Support Multiple AAVMC Competency Domains: A Survey of Shelter Medicine Programming at AVMA-Accredited Colleges
authors: Dalrymple AM, DeTar LG, Weisent J, Kreisler RE
citation: Dalrymple AM, DeTar LG, Weisent J, Kreisler RE Shelter Medicine Programs Support Multiple AAVMC Competency Domains: A Survey of Shelter Medicine Programming at AVMA-Accredited Colleges. Journal of Veterinary Medical Education. 2026. doi:10.3138/jvme-2024-0105
abstract: This study evaluated shelter medicine education availability at 54 AVMA-accredited veterinary colleges. Researchers distributed a 24-question survey from July–September 2023, receiving 43 responses (80% response rate). Results showed 88% of institutions offered formal shelter medicine coursework, with programs typically established around 2012. The survey found colleges employed 118 shelter medicine instructors (median of 2 per institution), though only 5% held tenure positions. Notably, 21% of responding schools had discontinued their programs, primarily due to lack of faculty and lack of a relationship with a shelter. The median program addressed 7 of 9 AAVMC competency domains, with many institutions addressing all 9 domains. The study highlights both the breadth of shelter medicine education and its vulnerability due to precarious faculty appointment structures.

mcqs.q: A survey of 54 AVMA-accredited veterinary colleges examined shelter medicine education. Which finding shows the vulnerability of these programmes?
o: Most instructors held tenure, and few programmes had closed
Only 5% of shelter medicine instructors held tenure positions, and 21% of responding schools had discontinued their programmes, mainly for lack of faculty or of a shelter relationship
Fewer than half of colleges taught shelter medicine, and closures were due to student disinterest
mcqs.e: 88% offered formal coursework, and the median programme addressed 7 of 9 AAVMC competency domains.

title: Veterinary Student Skills Learned at an Access to Care Clinic: Beyond Medicine and Surgery
authors: Alvarez EE, Schultz K, Lygo-Baker S, Chun R
citation: Alvarez EE, Schultz K, Lygo-Baker S, Chun R Veterinary Student Skills Learned at an Access to Care Clinic: Beyond Medicine and Surgery. Journal of Veterinary Medical Education. 2025. doi:10.3138/jvme-2024-0034
abstract: The research examined how a two-week rotation at Wisconsin Companion Animal Resources, Education, and Social Services (WisCARES) affected veterinary student development. Of 97 respondents with background information, 70% had minimal experience serving diverse or low-income populations beforehand. Students reported significant improvements post-rotation: increased comfort levels and compassion when working with low-income or homeless pet owners (mean = 4.54 and 4.42 respectively), greater ease interacting with members of different race or ethnicity groups (mean = 4.21), and enhanced appreciation for human-animal bonds (mean = 4.42). The clinic experience positively influenced clinical confidence, financial communication abilities, and creative case management. Researchers concluded that providing students opportunities to lead cases with economically disadvantaged and racially diverse clientele strengthens their professional readiness and clinical self-assurance.

mcqs.q: Veterinary students completed a two-week rotation at an access-to-care clinic (WisCARES). What was reported?
o: No change in comfort with diverse clients, and reduced confidence
Improvements only in surgical skills
Increased comfort and compassion with low-income and homeless owners, and improved confidence, financial communication and creative case management
mcqs.e: Of 97 respondents, 70% had minimal previous experience serving diverse or low-income populations.

title: Evaluation of a Student-Led Community-Based Veterinary Clinic for Disabled Low-Income Clients: A Case Study of the University of Florida PAWS Program
authors: Otero DK, James TG, Stone AE
citation: Otero DK, James TG, Stone AE Evaluation of a Student-Led Community-Based Veterinary Clinic for Disabled Low-Income Clients: A Case Study of the University of Florida PAWS Program. Journal of Veterinary Medical Education. 2024. doi:10.3138/jvme-2023-0032
abstract: The study evaluated a student-led veterinary clinic serving disabled individuals with low incomes (the PAWS Program at the University of Florida). During 2020–2021, the program conducted 162 monthly appointments with approximately 15 veterinary students volunteering per clinic session. Key findings: clients attributed enrollment in the clinic with improved quality-of-life and reduction of financial burden, saving clients roughly $2,050 per pet annually. Students demonstrated positive attitude changes and increased readiness to provide care to people with disabilities and people experiencing low socioeconomic position. The clinic effectively facilitated core curriculum learning outcomes while addressing intersectional inequities in veterinary care access, underscoring the value of community health practice within veterinary education.

mcqs.q: The PAWS programme is a student-led clinic for disabled low-income clients. What did evaluation show?
o: Clients reported no benefit
Clients reported improved quality of life and saved about $2,050 per pet annually, and students showed positive attitude changes
Students became less ready to care for low-income clients
mcqs.e: The programme held 162 monthly appointments in 2020 to 2021.

title: Cultural Competence Is Everyone's Business: Embedding Cultural Competence in Curriculum Frameworks to Advance Veterinary Education
authors: Gongora J, van Gelderen I, Vost M, Zaki S, Sutherland S, Pye M, Quain A, Taylor R
citation: Gongora J, van Gelderen I, Vost M, Zaki S, Sutherland S, Pye M, Quain A, Taylor R Cultural Competence Is Everyone's Business: Embedding Cultural Competence in Curriculum Frameworks to Advance Veterinary Education. Journal of Veterinary Medical Education. 2023. doi:10.3138/jvme-2021-0113
abstract: The authors describe implementing a curriculum framework at the University of Sydney veterinary program that integrates cultural competence throughout veterinary education. As stated in the article, veterinarians work with culturally and linguistically diverse teams, clients, and communities. The framework encompasses defining cultural competence, perceptions of animals, effective communication, and community engagement in a range of contexts. Learning outcomes were aligned with course objectives and institutional graduate qualities. The approach employed constructive alignment by connecting outcomes to teaching activities and assessment, with vertical integration across the curriculum. The integration aligns with accreditation recommendations and evidence-based practices in medicine, nursing, and allied health disciplines.

mcqs.q: The University of Sydney embedded cultural competence throughout its veterinary curriculum. What does the framework include?
o: Only a single elective lecture
Only language teaching
Defining cultural competence, perceptions of animals, communication and community engagement, with constructive alignment and vertical integration
mcqs.e: Veterinarians work with culturally and linguistically diverse teams, clients and communities.

title: Evaluation of Population Management Based on Trap–Neuter–Return and Trap–Neuter–Adoption Practices in a Free-Roaming Cat Colony in the Federal District, Brazil
citation: Junqueira ANN, Galera PD Evaluation of Population Management Based on Trap–Neuter–Return and Trap–Neuter–Adoption Practices in a Free-Roaming Cat Colony in the Federal District, Brazil. Animals. 2024. doi:10.3390/ani14172478
abstract: This study evaluated the use of trap-neuter-return (TNR) and trap-neuter-adoption (TNA) in a free-roaming cat colony in Brazil's Federal District over 18 months involving 157 cats that had not previously been managed. The study had three phases: recognition and preparation, TNR/TNA intervention, and monitoring. Following interventions, there was a 47.8% reduction in colony size, and 98.8% of the animals were sterilized. Adoption played an important role in reducing population growth, preventing kitten birth, fostering stronger bonds between caregivers and animals, and protecting against death, disappearance, and abandonment. The study demonstrates that combining TNR with adoption (TNA) provides complementary population management benefits beyond sterilization alone.

mcqs.q: TNR and trap-neuter-adoption were combined in a Brazilian colony of 157 cats over 18 months. What was found?
o: Colony size increased
Only 10% were sterilised
Colony size fell 47.8% and 98.8% were sterilised, with adoption preventing births and protecting against death and abandonment
mcqs.e: The study had recognition, intervention and monitoring phases.

title: Four Years of Promising Trap-Neuter-Return (TNR) in Córdoba, Spain: A Scalable Model for Urban Feline Management
authors: Luzardo OP, Vara-Rascón M, Dufau A, Infante E, Travieso-Aja MM
citation: Luzardo OP, Vara-Rascón M, Dufau A, Infante E, Travieso-Aja MM Four Years of Promising Trap-Neuter-Return (TNR) in Córdoba, Spain: A Scalable Model for Urban Feline Management. Animals. 2025. doi:10.3390/ani15040482
abstract: The research documents Córdoba's citywide TNR initiative involving 225 groups of cats (usually named colonies) managed from 2020 onward. The program achieved 95% sterilization coverage while limiting population growth despite external pressures like abandonment and immigration from unmanaged areas. Key findings indicate an overall population decline of 2.68%, though modeling suggests this prevented approximately 70% population growth that would have occurred without intervention. Program costs averaged EUR 0.62 annually per resident. Population viability analysis projects a potential 55% reduction by 2028 with sustained implementation. The study emphasizes the initiative's integration of citizen science and adaptive management as a replicable framework for large-scale TNR initiatives in urban contexts addressing animal welfare, public health, and biodiversity conservation concerns.

mcqs.q: Córdoba, Spain, managed 225 cat groups by TNR from 2020. What were the results?
o: The population doubled
Sterilisation coverage was 95%, the population fell 2.68% while modelling suggests about 70% growth was prevented, and costs averaged EUR 0.62 per resident annually
Coverage was 20%
mcqs.e: The programme integrates citizen science and adaptive management.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of non-arsenical adulticide protocols using moxidectin and doxycycline for the treatment of adult heartworm infection in dogs
authors: Santiwattanatarm T, Sakcamduang W, Kongkaew C, Anothaisintawee T, Taechikantaphat M
journal: Current Research in Parasitology and Vector-Borne Diseases
citation: Santiwattanatarm T, Sakcamduang W, Kongkaew C, Anothaisintawee T, Taechikantaphat M. A systematic review and meta-analysis of non-arsenical adulticide protocols using moxidectin and doxycycline for the treatment of adult heartworm infection in dogs. Current Research in Parasitology and Vector-Borne Diseases. 2026;9:100372. doi:10.1016/j.crpvbd.2026.100372
abstract: Non-arsenical protocols combining moxidectin (topical) with doxycycline (oral) demonstrated time-dependent adulticidal effects against Dirofilaria immitis. This analysis examined six databases and grey literature through November 2024, including 14 studies with 358 dogs, primarily stage 1-2 disease. Comparative studies showed antigen-negative conversion rates comparable to melarsomine from 9 months forward, with strongest evidence at 18 months. Pre-post analysis revealed 99% of dogs achieved antigen-negative status by 12 months (95% CI: 99-100%, moderate certainty). Microfilaria counts declined rapidly post-treatment. The combination appears to be well-tolerated and represents a practical alternative when melarsomine is unavailable or contraindicated, though researchers note the need for additional high-quality randomized trials with extended monitoring.

mcqs.q: A meta-analysis of 14 studies (358 dogs) evaluated moxidectin plus doxycycline for adult heartworm. What was found?
o: Antigen-negative conversion occurred within 2 weeks, and melarsomine is not needed
Antigen-negative conversion was comparable to melarsomine from about 9 months, with 99% of dogs antigen-negative by 12 months, making it a practical alternative when melarsomine is unavailable
Fewer than half of dogs became antigen-negative at 12 months, so the protocol is not recommended
mcqs.e: Microfilaria counts declined rapidly, and the authors call for more randomised trials with extended monitoring.

title: Clinicopathological findings of FeLV- positive cats at a secondary referral center in Florida, USA (2008-2019)
citation: Pare, Ellis, Juette. Clinicopathological findings of FeLV- positive cats at a secondary referral center in Florida, USA (2008-2019). PLoS ONE. 2022.
abstract:
Objectives: The aim of this study was to describe the seroprevalence, presenting complaint, clinicopathological changes, co-morbidities and outcomes of feline leukemia virus positive cats presented to a specialty referral center in Florida, USA.
 
 Methods: In this retrospective study, medical records of 8050 cats presented to a private referral center from August 2008 to September 2019 were reviewed. Inclusion criteria required was a positive result for feline leukemia virus by point-of-care antigen testing or immunofluorescence assay.
 
 Results: Forty-one cases met the inclusion criteria. Of 2002 cats that were tested, 41 cats (2%) met the inclusion criteria. One cat had a negative point of care antigen test result and positive bone marrow IFA result. The mean age at diagnosis was 9 years. The main reasons for presentation were abnormal complete blood cell count results (35%), followed by pleural effusion (18%), and anorexia (15%). The most common laboratory abnormalities included anaemia (71%), of which 74% had a nonregenerative anemia, thrombocytopenia (52%), elevated aspartate aminotransferase (50%), hyperbilirubinemia (35%), and hypokalemia (35%). Seven percent of cats (3/41) were also positive for feline immunodeficiency virus. The most common diagnoses were neoplasia (76%) and bone marrow disorders (12%). Cats with neoplasia were significantly younger. Survival to discharge was 88%.
 
 Conclusion and relevance: Results of this study show that feline leukemia virus is uncommon in secondary referral center, even if this represents a population of unhealthy cats. The most common associated diagnosis was neoplasia, which was more likely to be seen in younger cats (< 4 years of age). The mean age of cats positive for feline leukemia virus was also older than previously published data. These findings support the current guidelines which indicate that cats presented with clinical illness should be tested for FeLV at the time of presentation.

mcqs.q: Forty-one FeLV-positive cats were reviewed at a Florida referral centre. Which laboratory abnormalities were most common?
o: Erythrocytosis and leukocytosis
Anaemia (71%, mostly non-regenerative), thrombocytopenia (52%) and raised aspartate aminotransferase (50%)
Hypoglycaemia and hypercalcaemia only
mcqs.e: The main presenting complaints were abnormal blood counts, pleural effusion and anorexia, and mean age at diagnosis was 9 years.

title: Prolonged persistence of canine distemper virus RNA, and virus isolation in naturally infected shelter dogs
citation: Allen, Ellis, Liang, Lim, Newbury. Prolonged persistence of canine distemper virus RNA, and virus isolation in naturally infected shelter dogs. PLoS ONE. 2023.
abstract: Canine distemper virus remains an important source of morbidity and mortality in animal shelters. RT-PCR is commonly used to aid diagnosis and has been used to monitor dogs testing positive over time to gauge the end of infectious potential. Many dogs excrete viral RNA for prolonged periods which has complicated disease management. The goal of this retrospective study was to describe the duration and characteristics of viral RNA excretion in shelter dogs with naturally occurring CDV and investigate the relationship between that viral RNA excretion and infectious potential using virus isolation data. Records from 98 different humane organizations with suspect CDV were reviewed. A total of 5,920 dogs were tested with 1,393; 4,452; and 75 found to be positive, negative, or suspect on RT-PCR respectively. The median duration of a positive test was 34 days (n = 325), and 25% (82/325) of the dogs still excreting viral RNA after 62 days of monitoring. Virus isolation was performed in six dogs who were RT-PCR positive for > 60 days. Infectious virus was isolated only within the first two weeks of monitoring at or around the peak viral RNA excretion (as detected by the lowest cycle threshold) reported for each dog. Our findings suggest that peak viral RNA excretion and the days surrounding it might be used as a functional marker to gauge the end of infectious risk. Clarifying the earliest point in time when dogs testing positive for canine distemper by RT-PCR can be considered non-contagious will improve welfare and lifesaving potential of shelters by enabling recovered dogs to be cleared more quickly for live release outcomes.

mcqs.q: RT-PCR was used to monitor canine distemper virus (CDV) in shelter dogs. What did virus isolation show about infectiousness?
o: Many dogs shed viral RNA for a long time (median 34 days), but infectious virus was isolated only within the first two weeks around peak shedding
Infectious virus was isolated from all dogs for over 60 days
RNA shedding stopped within 3 days in all dogs
mcqs.e: Twenty-five percent of dogs were still excreting RNA after 62 days of monitoring.

title: An Accessible Alternative to Melarsomine: “Moxi-Doxy” for Treatment of Adult Heartworm Infection in Dogs
citation: Jacobson, DiGangi. An Accessible Alternative to Melarsomine: “Moxi-Doxy” for Treatment of Adult Heartworm Infection in Dogs. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2021.
abstract: Canine heartworm infection, caused by the filarial parasite Dirofilaria immitis, represents a serious and expanding animal welfare concern that is expected to increase due to the effects of climate change and the COVID-19 pandemic. A body of evidence has emerged to support the use of a non-arsenical adulticide treatment protocol, using moxidectin and doxycycline to kill adult heartworms over a prolonged period. While a three-dose protocol using the arsenical drug melarsomine is currently the safest and most effective treatment for heartworm infection, this drug is not available in some countries and is inaccessible for many owners and animal shelters. Moxidectin-doxycycline (moxi-doxy) provides a viable alternative to no treatment at all, in cases where arsenical treatment is not possible. Based on current evidence, the most effective non-arsenical treatment regimen is doxycycline 10 mg/kg PO q 12 or 24 h for 28 days, combined with topical moxidectin at label dose. Moxidectin is repeated monthly until no antigen detected (NAD) status is confirmed. Sustained release injectable moxidectin, in combination with doxycycline, may provide an alternative in remote regions or in settings where significant compliance or accessibility concerns exist, but more studies are needed. In moxi-doxy protocols, doxycycline should be repeated annually until NAD. This review summarizes the safety and efficacy of moxi-doxy, addresses controversies surrounding this treatment approach, and provides detailed recommendations for treatment regimens and post-treatment testing.

mcqs.q: Melarsomine is unavailable in a shelter. What is the most effective non-arsenical regimen for adult heartworm described in a review of 'moxi-doxy'?
o: Ivermectin alone at preventive dose for one month, then stop
Doxycycline for 3 days, and moxidectin once
Doxycycline 10 mg/kg by mouth every 12 or 24 hours for 28 days, with topical moxidectin repeated monthly until no antigen is detected
mcqs.e: It is a viable alternative to no treatment when arsenical treatment is not possible, though three-dose melarsomine remains the safest and most effective.

title: Incidence and Predictors of Canine Parvovirus Diagnoses in Puppies Relocated for Adoption
citation: DiGangi, Craver, Dolan. Incidence and Predictors of Canine Parvovirus Diagnoses in Puppies Relocated for Adoption. Animals. 2021.
abstract: Animal relocation programs seek to balance the animal population and resources between source and destination communities to promote positive outcomes, though little objective evidence has been reported on their physical and behavioral implications. The objective of the current report is to describe the incidence and predictors of canine parvovirus (CPV) diagnoses in 8- to 19-week-old puppies reported by destination shelters participating in a large scale, long-distance, structured animal relocation program. The incidence of post-transport CPV diagnoses in the study population of 4088 puppies was 2.3%. The number of pre-transport vaccinations, length of stay at the source shelter, and time between pre-transport vaccination and transport was not associated with the expected difference in count of post-transport CPV diagnoses (p > 0.05), and was lower in those 13–17 weeks of age (IRR = 0.08, 95% CI = 0.02–0.34, p = 0.001), 18–19 weeks of age (IRR = 0.11, 95% CI = 0.02–0.80, p = 0.029), transferred in to the source shelter (IRR = 0.31, 95% CI = 0.10–0.96, p = 0.043), and transported in the summer season (IRR = 0.07, 95% CI = 0.01–0.53, p = 0.010). When basic biosecurity practices and vaccination protocols were in place, post-transport CPV cases in puppies were few, suggesting that the timing of transport should take into account factors other than the number or timing of pre-transport vaccinations.

mcqs.q: The incidence of parvovirus in 4,088 puppies relocated to destination shelters was studied. Which finding is correct?
o: Incidence was 50%, and vaccination timing was the strongest predictor
Incidence was 2.3%, and number of pre-transport vaccinations, length of stay at source and vaccination timing were not associated, but older puppies had lower incidence
Age did not matter
mcqs.e: Relocation programmes balance animal populations and resources between communities.

title: Impact of surgical preparatory rinses with isopropyl alcohol or water on perioperative body temperature in pediatric female dogs and cats
authors: Isaza D, DiGangi, Isaza N, Isaza R
citation: Isaza D, DiGangi, Isaza N, Isaza R. Impact of surgical preparatory rinses with isopropyl alcohol or water on perioperative body temperature in pediatric female dogs and cats. Veterinary Anaesthesia and Analgesia. 2021.
abstract:
Objective
 To describe the effects of presurgical preparation with an isopropyl alcohol or water rinse on the perioperative rectal temperature (RT) of puppies and kittens.
 Study design
 Randomized clinical trial.
 Animals
 A total of 48 intact female mixed breed puppies and 43 intact female Domestic Short Hair kittens aged 8–18 weeks.
 Methods
 All animals were premedicated with intramuscular buprenorphine (0.02 mg kg–1) and acepromazine (0.05 mg kg–1). Anesthesia was induced with intravenous propofol (4 mg kg–1 to effect) for puppies or ketamine (5 mg kg–1) and midazolam (0.25 mg kg–1) for kittens. RT was measured every minute for the first 15 minutes at the beginning of hair/fur removal, then every 5 minutes for 45 minutes (dogs) and 35 minutes (cats). All animals were prepared for surgery using a 1.6% chlorhexidine solution, then rinsed with either isopropyl alcohol (group CA) or water (group CW).
 Results
 Mean RT difference between the groups was not significant at any time point. The mean RT at 45 minutes for dogs was 35.9 °C and 36.0 °C in groups CA and CW, respectively (p = 0.74). The mean RT at 35 minutes for cats was 35.1 °C in both groups (p = 0.84).
 Conclusions and clinical relevance
 The use of either water or alcohol as a rinsing agent results in the same degree of perioperative temperature change. Other factors that contribute to perioperative hypothermia should be considered when choosing between these rinsing agents in surgical preparation of pediatric and small animals.

mcqs.q: Puppies and kittens were rinsed with isopropyl alcohol or water after chlorhexidine preparation. What was the effect on perioperative body temperature?
o: Alcohol rinses caused significantly lower temperatures
Water rinses caused significantly lower temperatures
No significant difference between alcohol and water rinses at any time point
mcqs.e: Mean rectal temperature at 45 minutes in dogs was 35.9 and 36.0 °C, and 35.1 °C in cats for both groups.

title: Seroprevalence of Toxoplasmosis among Shelter-Housed Felines in a Philadelphia Suburb
citation: Mitchell, Reinhard, Cole, Stefanovski, Watson. Seroprevalence of Toxoplasmosis among Shelter-Housed Felines in a Philadelphia Suburb. Animals. 2022.
abstract: Members of the Felidae family are the definitive host of the ubiquitous zoonotic parasite Toxoplasma gondii. Few studies have been conducted to determine the epidemiology of T. gondii in domestic felines within animal shelter populations. The goal of this study was to assess seroprevalence in a limited-admission shelter in the greater Philadelphia area. Serum samples were collected from cats at a shelter in Media, Pennsylvania during the summer of 2018 to assess the proportion of the population that was IgM or IgG seropositive for antibodies against T. gondii, using a commercially available ELISA. Out of the 84 cats that were sampled, 24 cats were seropositive, giving a population prevalence of 28.6%. Nine cats were seropositive for IgM, nine were seropositive for IgG, and six were seropositive for both IgM and IgG. Based on our data, we found that a large percentage of this population was seronegative. Although the sample size in this study was limited and prevented us from obtaining statistically significant results, this research can serve as a pilot study for further investigations into the seroprevalence of toxoplasmosis among shelter-housed felines.

mcqs.q: Serology of 84 cats in a limited-admission shelter near Philadelphia found 28.6% seropositive for Toxoplasma gondii (IgM, IgG or both). How should this result be interpreted?
o: Because 28.6% were seropositive, all cats in the shelter are shedding oocysts
A large proportion of the cats were seronegative and still susceptible, but the small sample makes it a pilot result
The result proves that shelter cats are at greater risk than owned cats
mcqs.e: Nine cats were IgM positive, nine IgG positive, and six both. The authors note that the sample size prevented statistically significant results.

title: A Pilot Study Examining the Experience of Veterinary Telehealth in an Underserved Population Through a University Program Integrating Veterinary Students
citation: Lundahl, Powell, Reinhard, Healey, Watson. A Pilot Study Examining the Experience of Veterinary Telehealth in an Underserved Population Through a University Program Integrating Veterinary Students. Frontiers in Veterinary Science. 2022.
abstract: Cost and transportation are two commonly cited barriers to accessing health care in both human and veterinary medicine within underserved communities. While human medicine has utilized telehealth as a means of breaking down this barrier, limited research exists to describe its use in veterinary medicine. The Pets for Life (PFL) program has partnered with the Penn Vet Shelter Medicine Program to provide veterinary appointments to clients, at no cost to the client, in underserved zip codes through virtual telehealth visits. These visits incorporated veterinary students as part of their clinical rotations through a service learning based model. Between January and August 2021, 31 PFL clients and nine veterinary students completed surveys to describe the role of telehealth in addressing barriers to accessing veterinary care, their perceptions of telehealth appointments, the human-animal bond, and changes in veterinary student empathy. PFL clients completed the survey immediately following their telehealth appointment, and veterinary students completed surveys prior to and following their participation in the PFL appointments during the rotation. Nearly 25% of clients reported that they would not have been able to secure transportation and 58% reported they would not have been able to afford an appointment at an in-person veterinary clinic. The population of clients who responded that cost was a significant barrier to accessing care did not entirely overlap with those who responded that transportation was a significant barrier to accessing care, indicating support for the use of telehealth in providing an alternative modality to address transportation challenges as a barrier to accessing veterinary care. Additional data suggests that both client and student experience was overwhelmingly positive, providing support for further service learning initiatives in veterinary student education. Further research is warranted to continue to assess the emerging role of telehealth in improving veterinary care for underserved communities.

mcqs.q: Pets for Life and Penn Vet offered free veterinary telehealth appointments in underserved ZIP codes, with students as part of rotations. What was examined?
o: Only surgical outcomes
Only laboratory tests
Telehealth's role in addressing barriers to care, client perceptions, the human-animal bond and changes in veterinary student empathy
mcqs.e: Cost and transportation are commonly cited barriers to care.

title: Understanding the Motivations of Foster Caregivers at Animal Shelters
citation: Ackerman, Watson, Serpell, Reinhard, Powell. Understanding the Motivations of Foster Caregivers at Animal Shelters. Animals. 2023.
abstract: Foster care programs in animal shelters have been shown to benefit animals and shelters, but little is known about what motivates foster caregivers to volunteer. This cross-sectional study explored the motivations and expectations of 131 foster caregivers from five shelters within the United States who completed a pre-foster survey between March 2022 and March 2023. The most common motivations were animal- or community-based, such as the desire to provide an animal with love or do something positive for the community. Ordinal logistic regression models were used to investigate associations between caregivers’ motivations and their prior foster experience, pet ownership history, age, gender, and foster animal species. The 18- to 29-year-old caregivers were most likely to expect companionship (OR 5.18, 95% CI 1.79–15.04), emotional support (OR 4.25, 95% CI 1.40–12.89), and to meet other community members through fostering (OR 5.04, 95% CI 1.85–13.74). Male caregivers were less likely to foster for emotional support than females (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.03–0.48), while dog caregivers (OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.04–4.76) and non-pet-owners (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.17–6.05) had greater odds of expecting companionship. This study highlights the importance of animal- and community-related benefits for foster caregivers and provides useful direction for shelters wanting to increase recruitment to expand their foster care programs.

mcqs.q: A survey of 131 foster caregivers examined motivations. Which finding is correct?
o: Common motivations were animal- or community-based, and 18- to 29-year-olds were most likely to expect companionship and emotional support
Motivations were mostly financial
Older caregivers expected more emotional support
mcqs.e: Male caregivers were less likely to foster for emotional support.

title: Returning a Shelter Dog: The Role of Owner Expectations and Dog Behavior
authors: Powell, Lee, Reinhard, Morris, Satriale, Serpell, Watson
citation: Powell, Lee, Reinhard, Morris, Satriale, Serpell, Watson. Returning a Shelter Dog: The Role of Owner Expectations and Dog Behavior. Animals. 2022.
abstract: Millions of animals are adopted from animal shelters in the United States each year, although some are returned post-adoption, which can decrease both the animals’ chances of future adoptions and the owners’ willingness to adopt again. In this study, we investigated the impact of adopter expectations for ownership and animal behavioral problems on post-adoptive dog returns at a large animal shelter in South Carolina. Between June–September 2021, 132 dog adopters completed a survey about their expectations for ownership through Qualtrics. Twenty-nine adopters returned their dogs to the shelter within three months of adoption, with a median length of ownership of eight days. Owners completed follow-up questionnaires about their perceptions of adoption and dog behavior at two days, two weeks, and four months post-adoption. Categorical principal component analysis revealed three factors pertaining to adopters’ expectations for ownership. Independent t-tests showed returning owners had significantly higher expectations for dog behavior and health (t = −2.32, p = 0.02) and the human–dog bond compared with non-returning owners (t = −2.36, p = 0.02). Expectations for ownership responsibilities did not differ between the groups. Two-thirds of adopters experienced dog behavioral problems post-adoption, although training difficulty decreased significantly between two days and four months (F = 5.22, p = 0.01) and nonsocial fear decreased between two weeks and four months post-adoption (X2 = 10.17, p = 0.01).
